docs.title: CILMUMBAI
docs.text:
Plans and starter code for the Claude Impact Lab Mumbai hackathon (21 November 2026) on civic budget and accountability.

Folder What it is mumbai-civic-platform/ Start here. The final recommendation, Aamcha Hishob (आमचा हिशोब): one knowledge graph of Mumbai's civic data with a search and intelligence layer, data catalogue, ontology and implementation plan. aamcha-hishob-specs/ How to build it. Spec-driven development plan: constitution, process, milestones, and thirteen full specifications with requirements, acceptance criteria and task cards. app/ The implementation, built spec by spec. SPEC-001 to SPEC-009 and SPEC-011 are built and tested: the intake desk has read real documents end to end, real BMC ward boundaries load into the place spine, the graph answers "where did the money for this road go" with sources and gaps, SPEC-007 puts it all behind one API with access tiers and a citation check, the citizen desk (SPEC-008) answers residents in Marathi, Hindi or English from it, the workflow engine (SPEC-009) runs the pipeline with review gates that only a reviewer can pass, and the audit desk (SPEC-011) writes challenged, sourced ward findings that code checks before a reviewer releases them. mumbai-civic-graph/ The first slice in detail: five idea plans, tender portal reference, the multi-agent system, and working starter code (agent definitions, session client, LangGraph pipeline). mumbai-civic-ideas/ Forty-one ideas rated for value and feasibility, including a full plan for the BMC and SRA redevelopment dispute.

Status: design documents, plus starter code that has been syntax-checked and dry-run but not run against the Claude API or a real database.

docs.title: Documentation site
docs.text:
The same documents are published as a website with MkDocs (Material theme) at https://akashtalole.github.io/CILMUMBAI/.

pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs serve            # preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000

docs/ holds symlinks to the folders above, so files stay where they are. A GitHub Actions workflow builds the site in strict mode on pull requests and, on every push to main, publishes it to the gh-pages branch. To turn the site on once: Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages / root.

docs.title: Aamcha Hishob: spec-driven development plan
docs.text: How to build the final solution, Aamcha Hishob, one specification at a time.

docs.title: Why spec-driven
docs.text:
Most of this platform will be written with AI coding agents, and most of its risk is in getting a fact, a citation or a permission wrong. Both are reasons to write down, before any code, exactly what each part must do and how we will know it does it. In this plan:

  • The spec is the source of truth. Code, tests and agent prompts are derived from it. When they disagree, the spec is fixed first, then the code.
  • Every requirement is testable. Requirements are written so that a test can pass or fail against them, and every acceptance criterion maps to a test.
  • Principles are enforced, not hoped for. A short constitution lists what may never be broken (no fact without a source, no agent writes to the graph, and so on). Every spec names the articles it touches and how it upholds them.
  • Small, ordered slices. Each spec is a vertical piece that can be built, tested and demonstrated on its own, in dependency order.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: File Contents 00-constitution.md Twelve non-negotiable principles, each with how it is checked 01-process.md The workflow from idea to release, definitions of ready and done, how Claude Code and reviewers take part, change control 02-spec-index.md Every spec, its milestone, dependencies and status; the dependency graph; target code layout 03-milestones.md What each milestone delivers, its exit criteria and the demo that proves it specs/ The specifications. docs.text: All specs are Draft. None has been reviewed by a second person, and no implementation exists beyond the starter code. The first step in 01-process.md is to review SPEC-001 to SPEC-005 together and move them to Ready.

docs.title: Constitution
docs.text:
Twelve principles that every spec, every change and every agent must uphold. A spec may not override them. Changing one needs the agreement of the product lead, the lawyer and one engineer, and a written reason in the change log.

Each article states how it is checked. If an article cannot be checked automatically, the check is named in the definition of done.

# Principle Checked by C1 No source, no fact. Every node and relationship carries a source document, page, verbatim quote, tier and confidence. Loader rejects records without them (SPEC-003); schema test C2 Quotes are verified in code. A fact whose quote does not appear on its cited page is held, not loaded. Scanned pages without a text layer are loaded only with a visible scan_unchecked mark. Loader quote check and its tests (SPEC-003) C3 No answer without citations. Every amount, date, identifier and proper name in an answer must appear in a cited fact; otherwise the system says the records do not show it. Citation checker (SPEC-007); question evaluation set (SPEC-012) C4 Agents do not write or publish. No agent has a tool that writes to a store, sends a message to the public, or publishes. Agents produce files; code validates and loads them; people release. Agent definition lint in CI (SPEC-012); tool inventory review C5 Records, not verdicts. Findings describe what records show. No content states or implies wrongdoing by a named party. Officials appear by post. Banned-word check; Challenger review; lawyer release (SPEC-011) C6 People release what names a party. Anything that names a contractor, developer, official post or elected representative in a finding passes a human release step. Workflow gate cannot be bypassed (SPEC-009) C7 No private individuals. The platform stores no names, phone numbers, addresses, faces or number plates of private individuals. Residents' input is redacted before storage and before any model call. Redaction tests; storage scans (SPEC-008, later SPEC-019) C8 Access tiers are enforced in the query layer. Every read carries a tier; nothing returns data above the caller's tier, whichever path it takes. Tier tests on every endpoint and tool (SPEC-007) C9 The archive and ledger are the record. Source documents are immutable; facts are append-only; every other store can be dropped and rebuilt. Rebuild test (SPEC-003, SPEC-006) C10 Three languages as equals. Marathi, Hindi and English are tested separately. A change that improves one and worsens another does not ship. Evaluation reported by language (SPEC-012) C11 Every behaviour change is evaluated. Changes to prompts, agents, rules, ontology or retrieval pass the evaluation gate before production. Promotion gate in CI (SPEC-012) C12 Simplest thing that meets the spec. No new service, store or framework without an ADR. Prefer deterministic code to a model call, and a model call to an agent. Design review; ADR required for new components

docs.title: Applying the constitution in a spec
docs.text: Each spec has a section Constitution that lists the articles it touches and, for each, the requirement or test that upholds it. A reviewer rejects a spec that touches an article without saying how.

docs.title: Change log
docs.text: Date Change Agreed by 16 Nov 2026 First version Draft, not yet agreed

docs.title: 1. The workflow
docs.text:
idea or need
      │
      ▼
 1 SPECIFY   write spec.md from the template: problem, stories, requirements, acceptance criteria
      │
      ▼
 2 CLARIFY   list open questions; answer them or mark them as assumptions with an owner
      │
      ▼
 3 REVIEW    a second engineer and the domain or legal owner review → status Ready
      │
      ▼
 4 PLAN      design notes in the spec: interfaces, data contracts, choices, risks
      │
      ▼
 5 TASKS     break into task cards, each ≤ 1 day, each verifying named requirements
      │
      ▼
 6 TEST      write the tests for the acceptance criteria first; they fail
      │
      ▼
 7 BUILD     implement task by task (people or Claude Code), smallest change that passes
      │
      ▼
 8 VERIFY    CI: unit, contract, integration, constitution checks, evaluation gate
      │
      ▼
 9 DEMO      show the acceptance criteria working to the spec's owner
      │
      ▼
10 RELEASE   merge, deploy to staging, promote → status Done; update the index

A spec moves through these statuses: Draft → Ready → In progress → Done, or Superseded when replaced. Only Ready specs may be built.

docs.title: 2. Writing requirements
docs.text:
Requirements use the EARS patterns so each one is testable:

Pattern Form Example Ubiquitous The system shall … The loader shall record the extractor version on every fact. Event When …, the system shall … When a record's quote is not found on its page, the loader shall write it to the held file. State While …, the system shall … While a workflow is paused for review, the system shall not publish its outputs. Unwanted If …, then the system shall … If the caller has no tier, then the API shall treat the caller as public. Optional Where …, the system shall … Where a page has no text layer, the loader shall mark the fact scan_unchecked.

Each requirement has an id (R1, R2, …) unique within its spec. Across the project it is written SPEC-003/R4.

Acceptance criteria use Given / When / Then, have ids (AC1, …), and name the requirements they verify. Each becomes at least one automated test, named after it (test_spec003_ac2_…).

docs.title: Definition of ready (spec)
docs.text:
• Problem, stories and scope are written; out-of-scope is explicit.
  • Every requirement is testable and has at least one acceptance criterion.
  • Constitution articles touched are listed with how each is upheld.
  • Interfaces and data contracts are concrete enough to write a contract test.
  • Dependencies are Done or have a stub contract.
  • Open questions are answered or recorded as assumptions with an owner.
  • Reviewed by a second engineer, and by the lawyer if C5 or C6 is touched, or the language reviewer if C10 is touched.

docs.title: Definition of done (spec)
docs.text:
• All acceptance criteria pass as automated tests in CI.
  • Constitution checks pass; any manual check is recorded in the pull request.
  • Evaluation gate passes where the spec changes behaviour (C11).
  • Documentation updated: the spec's status, the index, and any user-facing text in all three languages.
  • Demonstrated to the spec's owner.
  • No open task cards.

docs.title: 4. Traceability
docs.text:
Constitution article ─► Spec requirement (SPEC-nnn/Rn) ─► Acceptance criterion (ACn)
                                   │                               │
                                   ▼                               ▼
                             Task card (Tn) ──► Pull request ──► Test (test_specnnn_acn_*)
  • Commit messages and pull request titles start with the task id: SPEC-003/T4: quote check for text-layer pages.
  • A CI job lists every acceptance criterion in Ready or In-progress specs and fails if one has no test with its name once the spec is marked Done.
  • The index shows, per spec, how many acceptance criteria have passing tests.

docs.title: 5. Building with Claude Code
docs.text:
Claude Code works well from specs because the spec carries the context a fresh session would otherwise lack. The rules:

  1. One task card per session. Give it the spec file and the task id. It reads the spec, the constitution and the files the card names.
  2. Tests first. It writes or updates the tests for the acceptance criteria the card verifies, runs them to see them fail, then implements.
  3. Stay inside the card. If the card turns out wrong or the spec is ambiguous, it stops and proposes a spec change instead of improvising.
  4. No new components without an ADR (C12).
  5. A person reviews every pull request. For C5, C6 or C7 changes, the named reviewer must approve.

A starting instruction for the implementation repository's CLAUDE.md:

This repository is built from specs in aamcha-hishob-specs/.
- Read 00-constitution.md before any change. Never break an article.
- Work on one task card at a time. Read its spec in full first.
- Write or update tests named after the acceptance criteria before code.
- If the spec is unclear or wrong, stop and propose a change to the spec.
- Do not add services, stores or frameworks without an ADR.
- Commit messages start with the task id, e.g. SPEC-003/T4.

Agent prompts and rubrics are specified the same way: the spec states what the agent must and must not do, and the evaluation sets in SPEC-012 are its acceptance tests.

docs.title: 6. Branching, review and CI
docs.text: Step Rule Branch One branch per task card or small group of cards in one spec Pull request Links the spec and task ids; lists the acceptance criteria now passing Review One engineer always; lawyer for C5/C6; language reviewer for C10; data owner for ontology changes CI on pull request Lint and types; unit tests; contract tests; constitution checks; docs build; evaluation gate for behaviour changes Merge Squash; status of the spec updated in the same PR when it changes Deploy Main deploys to staging; promotion to production is a manual approval after the evaluation report

docs.title: 7. Changing a spec
docs.text:
• Small clarifications that do not change behaviour: edit, note in the spec's change log.
  • Behaviour changes: a pull request to the spec, reviewed like code, before the code changes.
  • A spec that is replaced is marked Superseded by SPEC-nnn and kept.
  • Constitution changes follow the rule in 00-constitution.md.

docs.title: 8. Cadence
docs.text: When What Daily, during a milestone Pick task cards; push; review Weekly Spec review: move Drafts to Ready for the next milestone; check the index End of milestone Demo against exit criteria in 03-milestones.md; retro; update the plan

docs.title: Milestones
docs.text: Dates assume the event on 21 November 2026. Durations after the event are estimates and depend most on how quickly data can be obtained.

docs.title: M0: Foundations (16 to 20 November)
docs.text:
Goal. A corpus for one ward is archived, read by agents, checked in code and held as a facts ledger.

Specs 001, 002, 003, 004, 005 Runs on A laptop: Docker Compose with Neo4j, Postgres and MinIO; Claude API with event credits Data One ward: fifty tenders with notices, roads budget pages for five years, ward and road geometry, the ward office's posts

Exit criteria

  • Every document in the corpus is in the archive with hash and metadata.
  • One intake run produces a facts file; the loader accepts or holds every record with a stated reason.
  • At least 90% of extracted fields correct on ten hand-labelled documents.
  • The ledger can be replayed into an empty graph and produces the same node and edge counts.

Demo. Drop a new tender PDF in; watch it archived, read, checked and appear as facts with their quotes.

docs.title: M1: Hackathon slice (21 November)
docs.text:
Goal. Residents and judges can use three things on one ward, with correct, cited answers.

Specs 006, 007, 008, 009, 010, 011, 012 (minimum parts) Runs on The same laptop; a tunnel or a small host for judges' phones if allowed

Exit criteria

  • A judge picks a road in the ward and gets its works, contractor, cost and responsible post, each with a source.
  • A question in Marathi and one in English are answered with citations that pass the citation check.
  • One audit run produces a ward brief and one case file with its challenge review, paused for release.
  • A street alert fires for a new tender in a saved area.
  • The question evaluation set (thirty questions at this stage) passes at the agreed threshold.

Demo. The script in ../mumbai-civic-graph/06-prep-and-day-plan.md, using only these features.

Cut line. If time runs short, drop SPEC-010 before SPEC-011, and SPEC-011 before SPEC-008. Never drop the citation check.

docs.title: Burn-down rules
docs.text:
• A milestone ends on its date with what is Done. Unfinished specs move to the next milestone; they are not half-released.

docs.title: SPEC-001: Document archive and registry
docs.text: Status In progress: all acceptance criteria pass in CI; awaiting second review and demo (started 16 Nov 2026 at the product owner's request, before review) Milestone M0 Owner role Data engineer Depends on ADRs 0001, 0022 Personas served All, indirectly; reviewers and researchers directly

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
Every fact on the platform must trace back to the exact document it came from, as it was when fetched. Portals change and remove files. Today the corpus is a folder of PDFs with no record of where or when each came from.

When done, every source document is stored once, unchanged, addressed by its content hash, with a registry entry recording publisher, origin URL, fetch time, language, page count and licence. Nothing can alter or delete an archived document.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As a reviewer, I want to open the exact document and page behind a fact, so that I can check it.
  • As a data engineer, I want to add documents from a URL, a local file or a person's upload, so that every source reaches the archive the same way.
  • As a researcher, I want to know when each document was fetched and from where, so that I can cite it.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 The archive shall store each document under a key derived from the SHA-256 of its bytes. R2 When a document whose hash already exists is added, the archive shall not store a second copy and shall add the new origin to the existing registry entry. R3 The registry shall record for each document: hash, publisher, origin URL or upload reference, fetched or received time, media type, size, page count, the scripts found in the text (for example Devanagari, Latin), and licence. R4 The archive shall not offer any operation that modifies or deletes a stored document. R5 When a document is added, the system shall emit an archive.document_added event carrying the hash and publisher. R6 The system shall accept documents from three routes: fetch by URL, local file, and upload by an authenticated contributor. R7 If a fetch fails or returns a non-document response, then the system shall record the failure with its reason and shall not create a registry entry. R8 Where a document is uploaded by a contributor, the registry shall record the contributor's account id and shall not record their name or contact details. R9 The system shall extract and store the text of each page that has a text layer, keyed by hash and page number.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 An empty archive A PDF is added from a local file It is stored at source/<publisher>/<yyyy>/<sha256>.pdf and a registry row exists with all R3 fields R1, R3, R6 AC2 A document already archived The same bytes are added from a different URL No new object is stored; the registry row lists both origins R2 AC3 An archived document Any client tries to overwrite or delete it The operation is refused; the stored bytes are unchanged R4 AC4 An archive with a subscriber to events A document is added One archive.document_added event with hash and publisher is emitted R5 AC5 A URL that returns an HTML error page It is fetched A failure is recorded with reason not_a_document; no registry row is created R6, R7 AC6 A contributor's upload It is archived The registry holds the account id and no name, phone or email R6, R8 AC7 A PDF with a text layer on pages 1 to 3 and a scanned page 4 It is archived Text for pages 1 to 3 is stored; page 4 is recorded as no_text_layer R9

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
class Archive(Protocol):
    def add_file(self, path: Path, publisher: str, licence: str) -> DocumentRef: ...
    def add_url(self, url: str, publisher: str, licence: str) -> DocumentRef | FetchFailure: ...
    def add_upload(self, data: bytes, filename: str, account_id: str) -> DocumentRef: ...
    def open(self, sha256: str) -> BinaryIO: ...
    def page_text(self, sha256: str, page: int) -> str | None: ...   # None when no text layer

Registry table registry.documents: sha256 PK, publisher, media_type, extension, size_bytes, page_count, scripts text[], licence, storage_key, first_seen_at. Table registry.origins: sha256, origin_kind (url|file|upload), origin_ref, fetched_at, account_id NULL. Table registry.pages: sha256, page, has_text_layer, text_key.

Event (JSON on the queue): {"type": "archive.document_added", "sha256": "…", "publisher": "bmc", "at": "…"}

Storage: S3-compatible bucket with versioning and object lock in governance mode (MinIO locally).

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• Adding a 20 MB PDF completes in under 10 seconds locally, excluding network fetch.
  • Fetching identifies itself with a generic client name and waits at least 5 seconds between requests to the same host.
  • Never bypasses logins or captchas; such pages are added by a person as files.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C1 Provides the document and page that every fact cites C7 R8: contributor identity stored as account id only C9 R4: archive is immutable; object lock

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Scheduled collection and change detection (SPEC-014). OCR of scanned pages (SPEC-005). Redaction of residents' images (SPEC-019).

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• Record the scripts found in page text (ISO 15924 codes such as Deva, Latn) by counting characters in each Unicode block. Telling Marathi from Hindi is left to the intake desk, which reads the text.
  • Text extraction with PyMuPDF. Store page text as separate objects under parsed/<sha256>/page-<n>.txt so the loader's quote check reads one page cheaply.
  • Object lock in governance mode allows an administrator to remove a document only through a documented legal process, recorded outside the application.

docs.title: SPEC-002: Ontology, shapes and generated schema
docs.text: Status In progress: all acceptance criteria pass in CI; awaiting second review, and Marathi labels await the language reviewer Milestone M0 Owner role Graph engineer Depends on ADRs 0005 Personas served Researchers; all, indirectly

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
The extractor agents, the loader, the graph and the documentation must agree on what kinds of things and relationships exist. Today the starter code parses a Markdown file for labels.

When done, the Mumbai Civic Ontology for the first four graphs (Place, Money, Procurement, Works and Assets, plus Organisation and Evidence) lives as Turtle and SHACL files, and a build step generates the extraction schema, the loader whitelist and the documentation from them.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As an AI engineer, I want the extraction schema generated from the ontology, so that agents can only emit types that exist.
  • As a graph engineer, I want one place to add a class or property, so that every component picks it up.
  • As a researcher, I want published, versioned definitions, so that I can interpret the data.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 The ontology shall define classes and properties for Place, Money, Procurement, Works and Assets, Organisation and Evidence, as listed in the platform's ontology document, with English and Marathi labels. R2 The ontology shall reuse or declare equivalence to OCDS, W3C Organization, PROV-O, SKOS, OWL-Time and GeoSPARQL terms where they exist. R3 SHACL shapes shall require on every fact the provenance fields: source document, page, quote, tier, confidence. R4 The build shall generate a JSON Schema for extracted records, a label and relationship whitelist with allowed domains and ranges, and a Markdown reference page. R5 The ontology shall carry a semantic version; the build shall embed that version in every generated artefact. R6 If the Turtle files are not valid, or a generated artefact differs from the committed one, then CI shall fail.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 The ontology files They are parsed with rdflib No errors; every class and property has rdfs:label in en and mr; every class with a counterpart in OCDS, W3C Organization, PROV-O, SKOS, OWL-Time or GeoSPARQL declares it R1, R2 AC2 A valid tender record with all provenance fields It is validated against the shapes It conforms R3 AC3 A tender record missing quote It is validated It fails with a message naming quote R3 AC4 The ontology The build runs schema/records.json, schema/whitelist.json and docs/ontology.md are produced, each stamped with the ontology version R4, R5 AC5 An edge FOR_WORK from a Contractor It is checked against the whitelist It is rejected because the domain must be Tender or Contract R4 AC6 A pull request that edits a .ttl file but not the generated files CI runs CI fails with "generated artefacts out of date" R6

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
app/ontology/
  mco-core.ttl  mco-place.ttl  mco-money.ttl  mco-procurement.ttl
  mco-works.ttl  mco-org.ttl  mco-evidence.ttl
  shapes/*.ttl   glossary.ttl   VERSION
app/src/hishob/schema/
  records.json      JSON Schema for one extracted record (node | edge | note)
  whitelist.json    {"labels": {"Tender": {"module": ..., "properties": {"estimated_cost": "integer", ...}}},
                     "edges": {"FOR_WORK": [["Contract","Work"], ["Penalty","Work"], ["Tender","Work"]]}}
app/ontology/REFERENCE.md   generated reference page

Each relationship is declared once per allowed pair with the annotations mco:edgeType, mco:edgeFrom and mco:edgeTo; each record property with mco:jsonKey and one or more mco:propertyOf. Annotations are used instead of rdfs:domain because RDFS reads several domains as an intersection, not a choice.

Command: hishob ontology build [--check].

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• Build completes in under 10 seconds.
  • Generated files are deterministic (sorted keys) so diffs are meaningful.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C1 R3: provenance fields required by shape C10 R1: Marathi labels required C12 One source of truth for types; no hand-maintained duplicates

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Land and Planning, People, Services, Voice and Law modules (later specs add them). A live SPARQL endpoint.

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• Start from the classes in mumbai-civic-graph/00-shared-foundation.md and mumbai-civic-platform/02-ontology-and-graphs.md.
  • Use pySHACL in tests and in the loader.
  • Ontology version: minor bump for additions, major for removals or renames. The loader refuses records stamped with an unknown major version.

docs.title: SPEC-003: Facts ledger and loader
docs.text: Status In progress: all acceptance criteria pass; awaiting second review and demo (started 16 Nov 2026 at the product owner's request, before review) Milestone M0 Owner role Graph engineer Depends on SPEC-001, SPEC-002 ADRs 0001, 0004 Personas served Reviewers; all, indirectly

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
Agents produce facts; nothing they produce may reach the graph unchecked. The starter loader checks quotes and writes straight to the graph, with no durable record of what was accepted.

When done, every batch of extracted facts passes schema validation and a quote check in code. Accepted facts are appended to an immutable ledger on S3; rejected ones go to a held file with a reason. Projections (SPEC-006) are built only from the ledger.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As a reviewer, I want every held fact with its reason, so that I can fix or discard it.
  • As a graph engineer, I want to rebuild the graph from the ledger, so that I can change engines or recover.
  • As a researcher, I want to know which extractor version produced a fact, so that I can judge it.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 The loader shall validate each record against the generated JSON Schema and the whitelist (SPEC-002). R2 For each record whose source page has a text layer, the loader shall confirm the quote occurs in the page text after normalising whitespace and Unicode (NFC). R3 Where the source page has no text layer, the loader shall accept the record with quote_check = scan_unchecked. R4 When a record fails validation or the quote check, the loader shall write it to the batch's held file with a machine-readable reason. R5 The loader shall append accepted records to the ledger as a new file and shall never modify an existing ledger file. R6 Each ledger record shall carry: fact id, kind, label or type, ids, properties, source sha256, page, quote, tier, confidence, quote_check, extractor id and version, ontology version, batch id, loaded time. R7 When a new record has the same identity as existing facts, the loader shall compare property by property: a property given a different value supersedes the fact that held it, a property not held before is added, and properties the record does not mention keep their earlier facts. The record is appended with supersedes listing the fact ids it replaces. R8 If a batch references an edge endpoint that exists neither in the batch nor in the ledger, then the loader shall hold that edge with reason dangling_endpoint. R9 The loader shall produce a batch report with counts accepted, held by reason, and superseded.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 A record with a label not in the whitelist It is loaded It is held with reason unknown_label R1, R4 AC2 A record whose quote appears on its page with different line breaks It is loaded It is accepted with quote_check = matched R2 AC3 A record whose quote does not appear on its page It is loaded It is held with reason quote_not_found R2, R4 AC4 A record citing a page with no text layer It is loaded It is accepted with quote_check = scan_unchecked R3 AC5 An existing ledger A second batch is loaded Earlier ledger files are byte-identical to before R5 AC6 An accepted record It is written All R6 fields are present R6 AC7 A tender in the ledger with a reference number and an amount A record with the same id and only a changed amount is loaded It is appended with supersedes listing the earlier fact; the current amount comes from the new fact and the reference number still from the earlier one R7 AC8 An edge to a node id not present anywhere It is loaded It is held with reason dangling_endpoint R8 AC9 A batch of 100 records with 5 bad quotes and 2 unknown labels It is loaded The report shows 93 accepted, 5 quote_not_found, 2 unknown_label R9

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
hishob load <facts.jsonl> --batch <id> --extractor <agent_id>@<version>

s3://…/facts/<graph>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/<batch>.jsonl      accepted, append-only
s3://…/staging/<batch>/held.jsonl                     {record, reason, detail}
s3://…/staging/<batch>/report.json                    counts

Held reasons: schema_invalid, unknown_label, unknown_edge, unknown_property, wrong_type, shape_violation, domain_range, unknown_source, page_out_of_range, quote_not_found, dangling_endpoint, label_conflict, unknown_ontology_major. Notes (kind: note) are never loaded; they go to staging/<batch>/notes.jsonl for a person.

Identity and fact ids:

  • Identity of a node is node|<label>|<id>; of an edge edge|<type>|<from>|<to>.
  • Fact id is a hash of identity, source, page and the canonical properties. Loading the same record again is a no-op counted as unchanged.
  • Same identity, a property with a new value: appended with supersedes listing the facts that held the changed properties (R7). Counted as superseded.
  • Same identity, only properties not held before: appended and counted as extended. This is how one tender split across several records (one quote each) builds up.
  • Same identity and the same values from another source or page: appended as corroboration; nothing current changes.
  • The index keeps, for every identity and property, the fact currently holding it (ledger.current_props), so every property can be cited to its own source.

The loader keeps an index of facts in Postgres (schema ledger) for supersession and endpoint checks. The index is derived from the ledger and can be rebuilt from it.

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• Loads 10,000 records in under a minute locally.
  • Deterministic: the same input produces the same ledger content apart from timestamps and batch id.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C1 R1, R6: provenance required and recorded C2 R2, R3: quote check, scan mark C4 The loader, not an agent, writes the ledger C9 R5: append-only; projections built from ledger

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Writing to the graph and indexes (SPEC-006). Review screen for held facts (SPEC-021). Fuzzy quote matching.

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• Reuse and harden load() and quote_on_page() from civic_client.py; read page text from SPEC-001 rather than reopening PDFs.
  • Normalise quotes and page text the same way: NFC (which also unifies precomposed and decomposed nukta letters, because those are composition exclusions), remove zero-width joiners, non-joiners and soft hyphens, collapse whitespace. Do not lowercase or strip punctuation: amounts and identifiers must match exactly.
  • SHACL runs once per batch, not once per record, to meet the speed requirement.
  • Fact id: hash of kind, label or type, node ids and source sha256 and page.

docs.text: Id Task Size Depends on Verifies State T1 Ledger writer and record model M SPEC-002/T4 AC5, AC6 Done T2 Schema and whitelist validation S T1 AC1 Done T3 Quote normaliser and check, with Marathi test fixtures M SPEC-001/T8 AC2, AC3, AC4 Done T4 Supersession S T1 AC7 Done T5 Dangling endpoint check against batch and ledger index M T1 AC8 Done T6 Batch report and command line S T2, T3 AC9 Done

How common is this in real BMC PDFs, and should such pages be treated like scans? AI engineer Measure on twenty real Marathi PDFs in M0; until then, a page whose text has Devanagari letters mixed with stray Latin-1 characters is treated as scan_unchecked

docs.title: Change log
docs.text: Date Change 16 Nov 2026 R7 and AC7 changed to property-level supersession after the first live intake run (SPEC-005): the extractor split one tender into two records, each with one quote, and whole-record supersession dropped the reference number from the current state. 16 Nov 2026 Implemented in app/src/hishob/ledger/ with the index in migration 002_ledger.sql; tests in app/tests/integration/test_spec003_*.py and app/tests/unit/test_quotes.py. Added hold reasons, the identity and fact-id rules, notes handling and an index rebuild (see section 5). Measured: 10,000 single-node records load in about 21 seconds locally. Ledger records carry a seq field giving their order within a file, used by the rebuild.

docs.title: SPEC-004: Place spine
docs.text: Status In progress: AC1 to AC5 pass; AC6 (field test by someone who knows the ward) and K/West's real roads are pending Milestone M0 Owner role Data engineer Depends on SPEC-002, SPEC-003 ADRs 0006, 0015 Personas served Sunita, Imran, Lata, Assistant Engineer

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
Almost every question starts with a place: a road, a lane, a ward. Tenders name roads in free text, in two scripts, with local aliases. Without a spine of places, nothing joins.

When done, the demo ward's administrative and electoral boundaries and named roads are loaded as facts with geometry, with aliases in Marathi and English, and two functions work: find a place by name, and find what is at a point.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As a resident, I want to name my road the way I say it, so that the platform finds it.
  • As the intake desk, I want road names in tenders matched to road ids, so that works land on the map.
  • As an engineer in the ward, I want a pin to resolve to the right road and ward.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 The system shall hold administrative wards, electoral wards and named road segments for the demo ward as ledger facts with geometry. R2 Each road shall carry its OpenStreetMap way ids, an English name, a Marathi name where known, and aliases. R3 find_place(text) shall return candidate places ranked by match quality, matching across scripts by transliteration. R4 at_point(lat, lon) shall return the nearest road segment within 50 metres, its administrative ward and electoral ward, and the distance. R5 If no road lies within 50 metres, then at_point shall return the wards only and state that no road was found. R6 When a reviewer confirms an alias, the system shall add it as a fact with tier derived and the reviewer's decision as source.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 The spine is loaded Ward and road counts are queried They match the source files R1 AC2 A road known as "S.V. Road" with Marathi name "एस. व्ही. रोड" find_place("SV road") and find_place("एस व्ही रोड") are called Both return that road first R2, R3 AC3 A point 10 m from a road at_point is called It returns that road, the right wards and a distance under 15 m R4 AC4 A point in a park 200 m from any road at_point is called It returns the wards and road: null with a reason R5 AC5 A reviewer confirms "Station Road" as an alias of a segment The decision is saved find_place("Station Road") returns that segment R6 AC6 Twenty test points chosen by someone who knows the ward at_point is called for each At least 19 return the road and ward they expect R4

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
def find_place(text: str, kinds: set[str] | None = None, limit: int = 10) -> list[PlaceMatch]: ...
def at_point(lat: float, lon: float) -> PointResult: ...

PostGIS tables in schema geo, populated from the ledger: admin_wards, electoral_wards, road_segments, aliases.

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• at_point under 50 ms; find_place under 100 ms.
  • Geometry in WGS 84; distances computed in a metric projection.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C1 Places are ledger facts with sources (boundary files, OpenStreetMap extract with date) C10 Marathi names and cross-script matching tested

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Plots and survey numbers (SPEC-027). Other wards beyond the demo ward (M2).

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• Names are matched on a normalised form (lower case, punctuation removed, runs of single letters joined, so "S. V. Road" and "SV road" agree) and on a Latin key made by transliterating Devanagari, so "अंधेरी" also matches "Andheri". Trigram similarity in Postgres ranks the candidates.
  • Record the OpenStreetMap extract date as the source's fetched time and licence as ODbL.

docs.title: Decisions made while building (16 Nov 2026)
docs.text:
• Sources. Administrative wards: DataMeet's Municipal_Spatial_Data/Mumbai/BMC_Wards.geojson (24 wards; licence not stated in the files reached, to confirm). Roads: an OpenStreetMap export in Overpass JSON. Electoral wards: no reachable source yet; any GeoJSON with a ward number imports.
  • Files are archived first. Each source file goes into the archive (SPEC-001); its places become ledger facts citing it, with the feature's name as the quote, and pass the loader's checks (SPEC-003). The geo tables are built from the ledger and can be rebuilt.
  • Tier. Community-digitised boundaries and OpenStreetMap are reported, not official.
  • Ontology 0.2.0. Adds name_mr on every node, an Alias node and an ALIAS_OF relationship, so a reviewer's confirmed alias is a fact like any other (R6).
  • What could not be fetched here. The build environment's connections to Overpass and Geofabrik are refused, so K/West's roads are not loaded yet. app/src/hishob/place/README.md gives the export query to run in a browser.

docs.title: SPEC-005: Intake desk
docs.text: Status In progress: all acceptance criteria pass (AC5 in the live test only); awaiting second review and demo Milestone M0 Owner role AI engineer Depends on SPEC-001, SPEC-002, SPEC-003 ADRs 0002, 0003, 0009 Personas served All, indirectly; reviewers directly

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
Reading hundreds of civic documents in two languages is the bulk of the work. The starter code defines an ingest lead with extractor, verifier and resolver agents on Claude Managed Agents, but it is untested and not wired to the archive or the ledger.

When done, a batch of archived documents is read by the intake desk, every document is extracted and independently verified, entity matches are proposed, and the outputs are handed to the loader (SPEC-003). The run is reproducible: agent versions, inputs and cost are recorded.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As a data engineer, I want to submit a list of archived documents and get back a facts file, a review file and a report.
  • As a reviewer, I want unsure entity matches and low-confidence facts listed, so that I decide them.
  • As the product lead, I want each run's cost and agent versions recorded.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 The desk shall accept a batch of archive hashes and mount each document, the generated record schema and a known-entities export as read-only files in the session. R2 The desk shall extract facts from every document using the record schema and shall have every document's facts checked by a separate verifier agent. R3 The session's sandbox shall have no outbound network access and no web tools; no agent in the desk shall have a tool that writes outside the sandbox. R4 The desk shall produce facts.jsonl, review.jsonl and report.md, where the report lists every input as covered or not covered with a reason. R5 The entity resolver shall merge organisations only on a hard identifier and shall never merge people without an official identifier; other candidates shall go to review.jsonl as unsure. R6 Where a page has no text layer, the extractor shall read the page image and mark facts from it with the page's scan status. R7 The runner shall record session id, agent ids and versions, input hashes, output file hashes, duration and cost, and shall hand facts.jsonl to the loader. R8 The session shall have a spending cap set at creation, and if it is reached the runner shall record the batch as incomplete rather than retry without limit.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 Ten archived tender PDFs A batch is run The session mounts ten documents, the schema and the entities file; all three outputs are downloaded R1, R4 AC2 A completed run Session events are inspected Each document has an extractor thread and a verifier thread R2 AC3 The agent definition files The CI lint runs No agent has web tools enabled, the environment allows no hosts, and no custom tool can write R3 AC4 A batch in which one PDF is corrupt It is run The report lists that file as not covered with a reason; the others are covered R4 AC5 Two contractor names differing only in "M/s" and "Pvt Ltd", no registration number Resolved They appear in review.jsonl as unsure, not merged R5 AC6 A scanned Marathi page It is extracted Its facts carry the page and arrive at the loader, which marks them scan_unchecked R6 AC7 A completed run The run record is read It has every R7 field and the loader's batch report is linked R7 AC8 A spending cap set very low A batch is run The run ends paused at the cap and is recorded as incomplete R8

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
def run_intake(hashes: list[str], *, ward: str | None, cap_usd: int) -> IntakeRun: ...

@dataclass
class IntakeRun:
    session_id: str
    agents: dict[str, str]          # name -> "agent_id@version"
    inputs: list[str]               # sha256
    outputs: dict[str, str]         # filename -> sha256
    status: Literal["complete", "incomplete", "failed"]
    cost_usd: float
    duration_s: int
    load_report: str | None         # path to SPEC-003 report

Agent files: app/agents/{ingest-lead,doc-extractor,fact-verifier,entity-resolver}.md, environment app/agents/environments/civic-cloud.yaml, rubric app/agents/rubrics/ingest.md. They are applied with hishob agents apply, which uses the SDK and a local, uncommitted lock file (app/agents/.lock.json) of ids, versions and content hashes. This replaces ant apply, which was not available in the build environment; the file format is the same, so ant apply can take over later.

Mounts: each document at /mnt/session/uploads/corpus/<sha256>.<ext> so extracted facts cite their source by hash; the generated records.json and the ontology reference at /mnt/session/uploads/schema/; known entities at /mnt/session/uploads/entities.jsonl. Run records live in agentkit.runs (migration 003_agent_runs.sql).

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• Field accuracy of at least 90% on the ten-document labelled set (SPEC-012 extraction set at M0 size).
  • A batch of fifty documents completes within the session's unattended time limit; larger batches are split by the workflow.
  • Readers use the smallest capable model; the lead uses the default model.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C1 Schema requires page and quote on every record C2 Loader checks every quote after the run C4 R3: no write, web or publish tools; lint in CI C7 Only public documents are mounted C11 Agent changes go through the promotion gate (SPEC-012)

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Scheduling and source watch (SPEC-014). Graph tools for intake agents (they get an entities file instead).

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• Move civic_client.py's ingest, upload, download_outputs and session loop into hishob.agentkit, with typed results and tests using recorded session event fixtures.
  • Integration tests against the real API run in a nightly job with a small cap, not on every pull request.
  • The workflow engine (SPEC-009) calls run_intake; this spec does not decide when to run.

docs.title: First live run (16 November 2026)
docs.text:
Four fixture documents: an English tender, a Marathi and English tender with a scanned page, an award notice naming one contractor two ways, and a damaged PDF. Session capped at $5.

Measure Result Status complete Cost and time $1.63 list cost; 351 seconds Threads 3 Document extractor, 3 Fact verifier, 1 Entity resolver Coverage 3 covered; the damaged PDF reported as not covered, with the reason Facts 39 records: 26 loaded, 2 held, 11 notes Quotes All 26 loaded facts matched their pages exactly Verifier Rejected an invented tender built from a resolution number, and the three edges that depended on it Contractor names "M/s Shree Ganesh Infra Pvt. Ltd." and "Shree Ganesh Infrastructure" kept apart and sent to review (AC5)

Findings to act on, each through the evaluation gate (SPEC-012) before any prompt changes:

  1. The extractor splits one entity into several records, one quote each. This exposed a loader bug: whole-record supersession dropped properties. SPEC-003/R7 now supersedes property by property; replaying this run's facts gives each tender both its reference number and its cost.
  2. The resolver is too cautious with public bodies. The rule written for contractors (merge only on a registration number) left three separate nodes for BMC. Public bodies and wards should match against a reference list: the place spine (SPEC-004) for wards, and a list of agencies.
  3. Wards without codes are held. The extractor named wards ("K/West Ward", "के पश्चिम विभाग") without the code the shapes require. With the place spine mounted as known entities, it can use the official codes.
  4. Nothing was extracted from the scanned page. The report says so. Reading page images is the next step for scans (ADR 0009).

docs.title: SPEC-006: Graph projection and named views
docs.text: Status In progress: AC1 to AC5 and AC7 pass on Neo4j 5.26; AC6 needs a Neptune instance Milestone M1 Owner role Graph engineer Depends on SPEC-003, SPEC-004 ADRs 0004 Personas served All

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
The ledger is the record, but questions need traversal. Applications and agents also need a small set of trusted, tested queries rather than free-form Cypher.

When done, the graph is built from the ledger by a projector that can run incrementally or from empty, behind a repository layer that works on Neo4j and Neptune over Bolt, and five named views answer the common questions.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As the API, I want named views with fixed shapes, so that answers are fast and consistent.
  • As a graph engineer, I want to rebuild the graph from nothing, so that I can change engines safely.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 The projector shall apply new ledger files to the graph in order, recording the last file applied. R2 The projector shall be able to drop the graph and rebuild it from the full ledger. R3 A superseded fact shall not appear as current in the graph; its history shall remain queryable. R4 Every node and relationship in the graph shall carry fact id, source sha256, page, tier and quote_check. R5 The repository layer shall expose these views: trace_money(node_id), who_is_responsible(asset_id, issue), work_status(work_id), ward_summary(ward), gaps_for(node_id). R6 All queries shall use only the openCypher subset agreed for Neo4j and Neptune, verified by running the view tests on both. R7 Where a view finds no data for a hop, it shall return that hop as an explicit gap rather than omit it.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 A graph built up to ledger file N File N+1 is projected Only its facts are applied and the watermark moves to N+1 R1 AC2 A populated graph It is dropped and rebuilt Node and edge counts and a hash of sorted fact ids match R2 AC3 A work whose due date was superseded work_status is called It returns the current due date and a history with the earlier one R3 AC4 Any node returned by any view Its properties are inspected Fact id, source, page, tier and quote_check are present R4 AC5 A road with a tender, award and contractor in the ledger trace_money is called It returns tender, award, contract and contractor in order, each with sources R5 AC6 The view test suite It runs against Neo4j and against Neptune (or its local emulation if unavailable) Both pass R6 AC7 A work with a tender but no budget head trace_money is called The budget hop is returned as a gap with the record that would fill it R7

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
class GraphStore(Protocol):
    def apply(self, ledger_files: Iterable[Path]) -> Watermark: ...
    def rebuild(self, ledger_root: str) -> RebuildReport: ...
    def view(self, name: str, **params) -> ViewResult: ...

@dataclass
class ViewResult:
    rows: list[dict]          # each item carries fact_id, source, page, tier
    gaps: list[Gap]           # {hop, record_needed, holder}
    query_ms: int

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• Each named view returns in under 300 ms on the demo ward.
  • Rebuilding a ward's graph from its ledger takes under five minutes.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C1 R4: provenance on every element C9 R2: rebuild from ledger C12 Named views instead of free-form queries

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Text and vector search (SPEC-017). Graph algorithms. HydraDB trial (tracked under ADR 0004, run against this suite).

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• Batch writes with UNWIND. Avoid vendor procedures. Precompute derived dates in the loader so queries compare plain values.
  • Neptune testing: run against a small development instance in the nightly job; if none is available at M1, run on Neo4j only and record the gap.

docs.title: Decisions made while building
docs.text:
• Shape of the graph. Every node has the label Node plus its ontology label, a unique id, its current properties and the provenance of the fact that last changed it. Each property's own provenance is stored as _prov_<property> (JSON), so a tender's cost and its reference number can cite different documents (SPEC-003/R7).
  • History. Every fact is also a Fact node, linked from its subject by HAS_FACT and to the facts it replaced by SUPERSEDES. work_status reads due-date history from these.
  • What has been applied. A Postgres table (graphstore.applied) records ledger files already in the graph; apply takes the rest in load order. rebuild empties the graph and applies everything, and the fingerprint (counts and a hash of fact ids) is compared.
  • Labels and relationship types are checked against the ontology before they are written into a query.
  • Speed on the test graph: median 4 to 28 ms per view.
  • AC6. The suite passes on Neo4j. A test checks no vendor procedures (apoc., gds.) or subqueries are used. Running it on Neptune waits for an instance (SPEC-030).

docs.title: SPEC-007: Query API, access tiers and citation check
docs.text: Status In progress: all acceptance criteria pass; awaiting second review and demo Milestone M1 Owner role Back-end engineer Depends on SPEC-006 ADRs 0014 Personas served All

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
Every surface (web, WhatsApp, agents, public API) must read through one layer that applies access tiers and checks citations. Otherwise one forgotten path leaks data or lets an uncited claim through.

When done, a single HTTP API serves places, named views and answers. Every request runs under a tier. Every answer that contains text composed by a model passes a citation check in code before it is returned.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As a resident, I want an answer whose numbers I can trust and check.
  • As the citizen desk, I want tools that return facts with ids I can cite.
  • As the platform, I want no path that bypasses tiers.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 The API shall expose GET /places, GET /point, GET /views/{name}, GET /facts/{id}, GET /sources/{sha256}/pages/{n} and POST /answers/check. R2 Every request shall resolve to exactly one tier: public, contributor, researcher, official or reviewer. R3 If a request carries no valid credential, then the API shall serve it as public. R4 The API shall filter every result by the caller's tier using tier labels on facts, before results leave the query layer. R5 POST /answers/check shall extract every amount, date, tender or bid identifier, survey number and proper name from an answer and confirm each appears in a fact the answer cites. R6 When the citation check fails, the API shall return the unmatched items and shall not mark the answer as checked. R7 Every fact returned shall include source sha256, page, quote, tier, quote_check and the date the source was fetched. R8 The API shall log each request with tier, endpoint, parameters and returned fact ids, and no personal data. R9 The API shall rate-limit public callers per address.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 The running API Each R1 endpoint is called with valid input Each returns 200 with its documented shape R1 AC2 No credential A view is called The response header shows tier public R2, R3 AC3 A fact labelled researcher-only A public caller requests a view that would include it The fact is absent; a researcher caller sees it R4 AC4 An answer "Contract value ₹4.2 crore, due 31 May 2026 [f1]" where f1 holds those values It is checked It passes R5 AC5 The same answer with "₹5 crore" It is checked It fails, listing "₹5 crore" as unmatched R5, R6 AC6 An answer in Marathi with amounts in Devanagari numerals It is checked against facts in Latin numerals Equal amounts match R5 AC7 Any returned fact Its fields are inspected All R7 fields are present R7 AC8 A request It is logged The log has tier, endpoint and fact ids and no phone, name or message text R8 AC9 A public client sending more than the limit Requests continue Further requests get 429 R9

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
OpenAPI document generated by the framework, committed, and checked in CI.

POST /answers/check
{ "text": "...", "cited_fact_ids": ["f1","f2"], "language": "mr" }
→ { "ok": false, "unmatched": [{"kind": "amount", "text": "₹5 crore"}], "matched": [...] }

Amount normalisation: lakh and crore, Devanagari and Latin numerals, "Rs", "₹" and "रु." are equivalent. Dates in any common Indian format.

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• p95 under 400 ms for views on the demo ward.
  • Citation check under 100 ms for a 300-word answer.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C3 R5, R6: citation check in code C7 R8: no personal data in logs C8 R2 to R4: single tier per request, filtered in the query layer

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Sign-in flows (Cognito wiring in SPEC-013; until then, tiers come from signed development tokens). Search endpoints (SPEC-017).

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• FastAPI; one dependency resolves the tier; the repository layer takes the tier as a required argument so it cannot be forgotten.
  • Proper-name extraction for the check: match against names of nodes in cited facts and the glossary; a capitalised phrase or Devanagari name not found there is reported as unmatched.

docs.text: Id Task Size Depends on Verifies State T1 App skeleton, tier resolution, development tokens M AC2 Done T2 Tier filter in repository layer; tier tests for every view M T1, SPEC-006/T6 AC3 Done T3 Endpoints for places, point, views, facts, sources M T2 AC1, AC7 Done T4 Amount and date normalisers with Marathi and Hindi fixtures M AC6 Done T5 Citation checker M T4 AC4, AC5 Done T6 Request logging without personal data S T1 AC8 Done T7 Rate limiting S T1 AC9 Done

docs.text: Date Change 16 Nov 2026 Implemented in app/src/hishob/api/; tests in app/tests/unit/test_citations.py and app/tests/integration/test_spec007_api.py. OpenAPI document committed at app/api/openapi.json and checked in CI. Run with uv run uvicorn hishob.api.app:serve --factory.

docs.title: Decisions made while building
docs.text:
• Which facts need which tier (app/src/hishob/api/access.py). Residents' own reports (trust tier citizen) and company, director and bid records need the researcher tier; documents residents upload need the reviewer tier. Everything else is public. A fact above the caller's tier is answered as not found, so its existence is not revealed.
  • Development tokens. Until Cognito (SPEC-013), tiers come from HMAC-signed tokens <tier>.<account>.<signature> keyed by HISHOB_TOKEN_SECRET. A missing, malformed or forged token is public.
  • Where filtering happens. Every view result passes through one function that removes nodes above the caller's tier and adds each node's quote and source fetch date. The repository layer itself does not take a tier yet; a test per tier rule covers this path.
  • Citation check coverage. Amounts (rupees, lakh, crore, Devanagari numerals, the precision the answer states), dates (English, Marathi and Hindi month names, numeric forms) and identifiers are checked in every language. Proper names are checked in Latin script only: there is no reliable way yet to tell which Devanagari words are names. Marathi and Hindi names are covered by the evaluation set (SPEC-012) until there is.
  • Logging. Free-text parameters (q, text) are logged as their length only.
  • Rate limit. In-process, per address, public tier only; behind several API tasks the shared limit is at the edge (ADR 0014).
  • Found while building: the geo build crashed on roads known only by name (from a tender) with no geometry. It now skips and counts them (SPEC-004).

docs.title: SPEC-008: Citizen desk
docs.text: Status In progress: all acceptance criteria pass, plus a live run; awaiting second review and demo Milestone M1 Owner role AI engineer Depends on SPEC-007 ADRs 0003, 0011 Personas served Sunita, Imran, Lata, Ramesh

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
Residents ask in their own words and language. They need an answer they can act on: who is responsible, what the records show, and a letter to send. The answer must never invent a fact.

When done, one agent answers a resident's question using only the API's tools, in the resident's language, with citations that pass the check, and drafts a complaint on request. Residents' messages are redacted before the agent sees them.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As Sunita, I want to ask in Marathi who will fix the drain in my lane and get a short answer and a letter.
  • As Imran, I want to know when the work on my road is due and who is doing it.
  • As Ramesh's community worker, I want to ask on his behalf and get something I can read aloud.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 The desk shall answer only from tool results returned in the same session. R2 The desk shall reply in the language of the question: Marathi, Hindi or English. R3 If the question needs a location and none is given, then the desk shall ask for one and shall not infer it from an image. R4 Every answer shall pass the citation check (SPEC-007); if a draft fails twice, the desk shall reply that the records do not show it and give the nearest facts and how to find out. R5 The desk shall name offices and posts, and shall name a person only if they are an elected representative. R6 Where a work on the asset is within a defect liability period, the answer shall say so with the end date and source. R7 Before any text reaches the agent, the system shall remove phone numbers, email addresses, house numbers and personal names other than those of public office holders. R8 The desk shall have read-only tools only, no delegation, and read-only memory.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 A question about a road in the graph It is answered Every figure in the answer appears in a tool result from the session R1 AC2 The same question in Marathi, Hindi and English Each is answered Each reply is in the question's language R2 AC3 "Who fixes the pothole outside my building?" with no place It is answered The desk asks for the location and states no office R3 AC4 A question about something the graph does not hold It is answered The reply says the records do not show it and names a way to find out; no invented figures R4 AC5 Any answer naming who is responsible It is checked It names a post and office; no official's personal name R5 AC6 A road with a work still under liability The resident asks about a defect The reply states the liability end date with its source R6 AC7 A message containing a phone number and the sender's name It is processed The agent's input contains neither R7 AC8 The agent definition CI lint runs Only read-only custom tools; no multi-agent block; memory attached read-only R8

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
def answer(question: str, *, language_hint: str | None, location: LatLon | None, tier: Tier) -> Answer: ...

@dataclass
class Answer:
    text: str
    language: Literal["mr", "hi", "en"]
    cited_fact_ids: list[str]
    check: CitationResult
    draft_letter: str | None
    gaps: list[Gap]
    session_id: str

Tools: find_entity, locate, trace_money, who_is_responsible, get_source, gaps_for, all answered by the worker through the API under the caller's tier.

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• Typical answer in under 30 seconds.
  • Session spending cap per question set at creation.
  • Routing (SPEC-017) will later send simple lookups to pages without the agent; this spec covers the agent path only.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C3 R4: citation check, fallback reply C4 R8: read-only tools only C5 R5: posts, not people C7 R7: redaction before the model C8 Tools run under the caller's tier C10 AC2: tested in three languages

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: WhatsApp and voice (SPEC-019). Filing complaints into government systems.

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• Start from app/agents/citizen-desk.md (moved from the starter code).
  • Redaction: rules for phone, email and house numbers; names found against a list of public office holders are kept, other personal names are replaced with a placeholder. Tested on a fixture set in three languages.
  • The two-attempt rule: the runner sends the unmatched items back once as a message to the session; on a second failure it returns the fallback reply built in code.

docs.title: 10. Tasks
docs.text: Id Task Size Depends on Verifies State T1 Move agent file; lint rules for the desk S SPEC-005/T2 AC8 Done T2 Tool answering through the API under tier M SPEC-007/T3 AC1 Done T3 Citation check loop and fallback reply M SPEC-007/T5 AC4 Done T4 Redaction with fixtures M AC7 Done T5 Location prompt behaviour; fixture conversation S T2 AC3 Done T6 Liability statement from who_is_responsible S T2 AC6 Done T7 Language tests and post-only naming tests in the question set M SPEC-012/T3 AC2, AC5 Done

docs.text: Date Change 16 Nov 2026 Implemented in app/src/hishob/agentkit/ (citizen.py, redact.py, language.py, tools.py) and app/agents/citizen-desk.md; tests in app/tests/unit/test_spec008_parts.py, app/tests/integration/test_spec008_citizen.py and app/tests/live/test_spec008_live.py.
