docs.title: Decisions made while building
docs.text:
• Tools read through the API, over HTTP, as the resident's tier. The desk cannot see what the resident could not.
  • Citations are markers. The agent writes [f_…] after each claim. Code strips them, runs the citation check, and builds the source list itself from the cited facts, so a source line can never be invented.
  • Review in code before anything is sent: citation check, reply language, no private person named, and the liability end date stated when there is one. One rewrite is requested with the problems listed; a second failure returns a reply built in code, in the resident's language, from what the tools returned and the gaps they reported.
  • Redaction removes phone numbers, emails, flat and house numbers, and names introduced as names or after an honorific. Landmarks are kept ("Shri Ganesh Mandir", "श्री गणेश मंदिराजवळ"), as are names on a keep list of office holders.
  • Memory is not attached yet: no memory stores exist. R8's read-only memory applies when they do.

docs.title: First live run (16 November 2026)
docs.text:
Question, in Marathi, with the resident's name and phone in it: who will fix the pothole on S. V. Road, and until when is the contractor responsible?

Measure Result What the model saw माझे नाव [name], फोन [phone]. … Tools called find_place, then who_is_responsible Reply In Marathi: the contractor must repair at its own cost until 31 May 2031; complain first to the Assistant Engineer (Roads), K/West, then the Executive Engineer (Roads), Western Suburbs; offers to write the letter Checks Passed on the first attempt; 8 facts cited Cost $0.05

docs.title: SPEC-009: Workflow engine and human gates
docs.text: Status In progress: all acceptance criteria pass with stubbed desks; no live run yet (the audit desk is SPEC-011) Milestone M1 Owner role Back-end engineer Depends on SPEC-003, SPEC-005 ADRs 0010 Personas served Reviewers, Advocate Nair

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
Work flows from intake to loading to audit to release, with people deciding at two points. Runs may wait days. The starter pipeline proves the shape in dry-run mode with a SQLite checkpoint.

When done, LangGraph workflows run in a worker, checkpointed to Postgres, started from queue messages, with human gates that cannot be bypassed and that survive restarts.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As a reviewer, I want a run to wait for my decision without losing its state.
  • As an engineer, I want to restart the worker without breaking runs in progress.
  • As the product lead, I want to see every run, where it is and what it waits for.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 The engine shall run workflow W1 (ingest, load, review if many held, audit each ward, release, publish) as a LangGraph graph. R2 The engine shall checkpoint state to Postgres after every step and resume from the last checkpoint after a restart. R3 The engine shall start runs from queue messages and from the command line, each with a thread id. R4 When the share of held facts in a batch exceeds a configured threshold, the run shall pause for review before audit. R5 While a run is paused at the release gate, the engine shall not copy any output to a public location. R6 Only an account with the reviewer tier shall be able to resume a run from a gate, and each decision shall be recorded with account id, time and reason. R7 Steps with side effects (starting a session, loading, publishing) shall be safe to repeat after a restart without duplicating their effect.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 A run of W1 with stubbed desks It runs to the release gate It pauses there with the expected state R1 AC2 A run paused at a gate The worker process is killed and restarted, then the run is resumed It continues from the gate with its state intact R2 AC3 A queue message {workflow: W1, thread: t1, ...} The worker receives it A run with thread t1 starts R3 AC4 A batch with 30% held and threshold 20% Loading finishes The run pauses at review; at 10% it proceeds to audit R4 AC5 A run at the release gate The public prefix is listed It contains nothing from that run R5 AC6 A run at a gate A contributor-tier account tries to resume it Refused; a reviewer can resume, and the decision row is written R6 AC7 A run killed just after the publish step started It is resumed Each output exists once in the public prefix R7

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
hishob workflow run <thread> --hash <sha256> [--hash …] --ward <code> [--ward …]
hishob workflow status <thread>
hishob workflow resume <thread> continue|stop|approve|hold|<ward,ward> --reason "…" --token <reviewer token>
hishob workflow retry <thread>
hishob workflow consume --queue-url <url> [--max N]

Queue message: {"workflow": "W1", "thread": "t1", "hashes": ["…"], "wards": ["K/W"]}.

Postgres, schema flow: LangGraph checkpointer tables; flow.decisions(thread_id, gate, decision, reason, account_id, decided_at); flow.steps(thread_id, step, result, finished_at) for completed side-effect steps.

Published outputs: published/<ward-slug>/<run_id>/<file> in the public store.

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• Restart to resumed in under one minute.
  • A paused run costs nothing while waiting.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C6 R5, R6: release gate, reviewer-only resume C4 Publishing is a code step after a human decision C12 One engine for all workflows

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Other workflows W2 to W8 (their specs add them on this engine). The review screen (SPEC-021); until then, the command line resumes runs.

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• Port orchestrator.py; replace the SQLite saver with the Postgres saver; replace dry-run stubs with run_intake, load and run_audit behind interfaces so tests stub them.
  • Idempotency: a session start records its session id before streaming; a resumed step reattaches instead of starting another. Publishing writes with a content hash key so a repeat is a no-op.

docs.title: 10. Tasks
docs.text: Id Task Size Depends on Verifies State T1 Port graph; step interfaces; stubbed tests M AC1 Done T2 Postgres checkpointer; restart test M T1 AC2 Done T3 Queue consumer and command line S T1 AC3 Done T4 Review threshold gate S T1 AC4 Done T5 Release gate, decision records, tier check M T1, SPEC-007/T1 AC5, AC6 Done T6 Idempotent session start and publish M T2 AC7 Partly: publish and completed steps are idempotent; reattaching to a running session is not built

docs.title: Change log
docs.text: Date Change 16 Nov 2026 Implemented in app/src/hishob/workflows/ (w1.py, live.py) and migration app/migrations/007_flow.sql; tests in app/tests/integration/test_spec009_workflow.py. Command: hishob workflow.

docs.title: Decisions made while building
docs.text:
• Steps behind a protocol. Steps has intake, audit and publish. Tests use stubs; LiveSteps uses the intake desk and real publishing. Its audit raises until SPEC-011 provides the audit desk, so W1 cannot yet run end to end on real documents.
  • Audits run in parallel, one LangGraph Send per ward, and wait together at one release gate.
  • The release gate takes approve (every ward), hold (none) or a list of wards. Holding ends the run with nothing published.
  • Two checks on resume. The command line refuses any token that is not a valid reviewer token before it connects to anything; Engine.resume checks the tier again and requires a non-empty reason, so no other caller can skip it. Every decision is written to flow.decisions.
  • Completed steps are recorded in flow.steps. When a run is retried, a finished intake or audit returns its saved result and is not called again.
  • Publishing is content-idempotent. Each file is copied with a write-if-absent. Copying the same bytes again does nothing; different bytes under the same key are an error, never an overwrite. A publish interrupted part way through finishes on retry with each file present once (AC7).
  • Thread ids are used once. Starting a thread that already exists is refused.

docs.title: Not done yet
docs.text:
• Reattaching to a running session. If the worker dies while the intake desk's session is still running, a retry starts a new session. The cost is repeated work, not duplicated facts, because the ledger refuses duplicates (SPEC-003). Recording the session id before streaming and reattaching to it is still to do.
  • Restart test is in-process. AC2 resumes with a new engine and new database connections, with nothing kept in memory. It does not kill an operating-system process, and the one-minute restart target is not measured.
  • No live run. That waits for the audit desk.

docs.title: SPEC-010: Street alerts
docs.text: Status In progress: all acceptance criteria pass; delivery by email is not built, alerts are read in the web app Milestone M1 Owner role Full-stack engineer Depends on SPEC-004, SPEC-006, SPEC-007 ADRs 0013, 0015 Personas served Imran, Lata, Farah

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
Residents learn about a road work when the barricades arrive. This is the platform's first application and the easiest for anyone to understand (idea 14).

When done, a resident saves an area and receives a message when a tender in it is published, awarded, changed by a corrigendum, or passes its completion date, each with the tender number and source.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As Imran, I want to know when work on my road is tendered, awarded and due.
  • As Lata, I want to know about anything tendered within 300 metres of our building.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 A contributor shall be able to save an area as a point with a radius between 100 and 1,000 metres, or as named roads. R2 When a tender, award or corrigendum fact is projected whose work is linked to an asset within a saved area, the system shall queue one alert per subscriber per event. R3 When a work's current due date passes with no completion fact, the system shall queue an overdue alert once. R4 Each alert shall state what changed, the tender number, the date and a link to the source page, in the subscriber's language. R5 The system shall not send the same alert to the same subscriber twice. R6 Where a work's location was matched from free text with confidence below a threshold, the alert shall show the tender title so the resident can judge.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 A contributor They save a point with radius 300 m The subscription is stored; 50 m or 2 km are rejected R1 AC2 A subscription around a road A new tender for that road is projected One alert is queued R2 AC3 A work due yesterday with no completion fact The daily check runs twice One overdue alert is queued R3, R5 AC4 An alert for a Marathi-speaking subscriber It is rendered It is in Marathi with tender number, date and source link R4 AC5 The projector replays the same ledger file Alerts are evaluated No duplicate alerts R5 AC6 A tender matched to a road with low confidence An alert is rendered It includes the tender title R6

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
account.subscriptions(id, account_id, kind, geom, radius_m, road_ids, language, created_at); alerts.outbox(id, subscription_id, event_key UNIQUE, payload, created_at, sent_at).

Delivery at M1: a page listing a subscriber's alerts (the Alerts tab). Email delivery needs an email service and the account store's contact details; it is not built. WhatsApp delivery comes with SPEC-019.

POST   /subscriptions     {kind: point|roads, language, lat?, lon?, radius_m?, road_ids?} -> 201; 422 bad radius or unknown road; 401 not signed in
GET    /subscriptions     the caller's saved areas
DELETE /subscriptions/{id}   204; 404 if not the caller's
GET    /alerts            the caller's alerts, newest first, rendered in each area's language, with source links
hishob alerts run         queue alerts for new tenders, awards and corrigenda (also run by `hishob graph apply`)
hishob alerts overdue     the daily overdue check

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• Alerts queued within 15 minutes of projection.
  • Subscriber contact details stored only in the account store, never in alert payloads or logs.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C1 R4: every alert links its source C7 Contact details isolated C10 R4: rendered in three languages

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: WhatsApp delivery (SPEC-019). Full web app (SPEC-020); a minimal sign-up page is enough for M1.

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• Evaluate on projector watermark changes: query new tender, award and corrigendum facts, join to assets with PostGIS within each subscription.
  • event_key = subscription id + fact id + kind, which makes R5 a unique constraint.

docs.title: 10. Tasks
docs.text: Id Task Size Depends on Verifies State T1 Subscription model and validation S SPEC-004/T3 AC1 Done T2 Event matcher on projector watermark M SPEC-006/T2 AC2, AC5 Done T3 Daily overdue check S T2 AC3 Done T4 Alert templates in three languages M AC4, AC6 Done (Marathi and Hindi wording to be reviewed) T5 Minimal sign-up page and email delivery M T1, T4 Page done (Alerts tab); email not built

docs.title: Change log
docs.text: Date Change 17 Nov 2026 Implemented in app/src/hishob/alerts/ (subscriptions.py, matcher.py, render.py), migration 008_alerts.sql, endpoints in api/app.py, the Alerts tab in app/web/, and hishob alerts. Tests in app/tests/integration/test_spec010_alerts.py and app/web/e2e/resident.mjs.

docs.title: Decisions made while building
docs.text:
• Matching runs on the ledger index and PostGIS, not the graph. An event is a Tender, Award or Corrigendum node linked to a work that improves a road. A saved point matches any segment of that road's name within the radius; a road subscription matches the road by name, so the several segments of one street count as one.
  • One alert per subscriber per event, not per fact. The key is the subscription and the event's node, so a later corrected cost on the same tender does not alert again. An overdue alert's key includes the due date, so an extended date that passes again is a new event.
  • No back-alerts. An event counts only if its node was first loaded after the area was saved, so a new subscriber is not sent a street's history. The overdue check is the exception.
  • hishob graph apply queues alerts after projecting, which keeps alerts within minutes of new facts (non-functional requirement). The output stays one JSON object, with alerts_queued added.
  • The saved area holds an account id and a place, nothing else. Alert payloads hold facts only; the subscriber's language lives on the area. Rendering happens when the alert is read.
  • Until sign-in (SPEC-013), the web app asks for the signed access code it was given, kept in the browser, or taken from a #token= link fragment, which is never sent to a server.

docs.title: Not done yet
docs.text:
• Email delivery, and contact details in the account store.
  • A daily scheduler for hishob alerts overdue (the deployment runs it from cron or a scheduled task; not wired).
  • The overdue check scans every work each day; fine for one city's works, to be indexed when it is not.
  • A work's location confidence comes from the IMPROVES edge's confidence. Alerts for assets other than roads, and for works matched to a ward only, are not yet generated.

docs.title: SPEC-011: Audit desk and release
docs.text: Status In progress: all acceptance criteria pass with scripted agents, plus a live run; awaiting review Milestone M1 Owner role AI engineer Depends on SPEC-007, SPEC-009 ADRs 0003, 0011 Personas served Farah, Arjun, Corporator Pawar, Assistant Engineer, Advocate Nair

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
The graph holds records; people need findings they can act on, and findings that name parties carry legal risk. The starter code defines an audit lead with a Challenger and a Drafter.

When done, an audit run for a ward produces a one-page brief, case files that have each been challenged, drafted complaints, RTI applications and meeting questions, and a gaps file. Nothing leaves the run until a reviewer releases it.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As Farah, I want three questions for Saturday's ward meeting, each with its source.
  • As the Assistant Engineer, I want the defects on roads still under contractor liability.
  • As Advocate Nair, I want each finding with its evidence and its challenge, so that I can release or hold it quickly.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 The audit lead shall read the graph only through read-only tools under the reviewer tier. R2 The run shall produce ward-brief.md, cases/, held/, drafts/ and gaps.jsonl as specified in the audit rubric. R3 Every case file shall be reviewed by a Challenger agent, whose review is stored beside it with a verdict of publish, publish with changes, or hold. R4 Case files with verdict hold shall be placed in held/ with the reason and not in cases/. R5 No output shall contain the words fraud, scam, corrupt, cartel, nexus or siphoned, or their Marathi and Hindi equivalents, or name an official other than by post. R6 Every amount, date, contractor and tender number in the brief and case files shall be followed by a source reference that resolves to a fact. R7 The run shall be graded against the ward-audit rubric and revised until it passes or reaches the iteration limit. R8 The outputs shall reach the public location only after a reviewer approves them at the release gate (SPEC-009).

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 The audit agent definitions CI lint runs The lead's tools are read-only; Challenger and Drafter have file tools only R1 AC2 A completed run for the demo ward Outputs are listed All R2 files and folders exist R2 AC3 Any file in cases/ Its folder is listed A .challenge.md with a verdict of publish or publish with changes is beside it R3 AC4 A case the Challenger held Outputs are listed It is in held/ with a reason and absent from cases/ R4 AC5 All outputs The banned-word and post-only check runs in code No violations R5 AC6 All outputs Source references are resolved through the API Every reference resolves to a fact, and the cited values match R6 AC7 A run whose first draft misses a rubric criterion The run continues Grader events show revision until satisfied or the limit R7 AC8 A completed run Before release Nothing from it is in the public location; after approval, the approved files are R8

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
def run_audit(client, http, ward, data, *, run_id, token, cap_usd=10) -> AuditRun: ...  # staging/<run_id>/
def check_outputs(files, http, *, token, private_names, contractor_names, keep_names) -> OutputCheck: ...
def arrange(raw_files) -> Arranged: ...   # places files by name and by the Challenger's verdict

hishob audit run K/W --api http://127.0.0.1:8000 [--run-id …] [--cap-usd 10]

Staging layout: ward-brief.md, gaps.jsonl, cases/case-NN-*.md with case-NN-*.challenge.md, held/ (each held case with its review and a .held.md reason written by code), drafts/{rti-NN,complaint-NN,questions}.md, manifest.json (the run record). Only files outside held/ and the manifest are offered for release.

Agent files: app/agents/{audit-lead,challenger,drafter}.md; rubric app/agents/rubrics/ward-audit.md.

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• A ward audit completes within the session's unattended time limit.
  • Spending cap per run set at creation.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C3 R6, AC6: references resolve and values match C4 Lead and specialists cannot write stores or publish C5 R3, R5: Challenger review; banned words and post-only check in code C6 R8: release gate C8 R1: reads under a defined tier

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Regulation desk and jurisdiction cards (SPEC-026). Contractor network views (later). Newsroom distribution (SPEC-031).

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• The output check in code runs after the session and before the release gate; a violation sends the run back to the lead once, then holds the file.
  • Marathi and Hindi banned-word lists are drafted with the language reviewer and the lawyer.

docs.text: Id Task Size Depends on Verifies State T1 Move agent files and rubric; lint S SPEC-005/T2 AC1 Done T2 run_audit on agentkit, tools under reviewer tier M SPEC-007/T3 AC2, AC7 Done T3 Output layout check S T2 AC2, AC3, AC4 Done T4 Banned words and post-only check in three languages M AC5 Done in code; the Marathi and Hindi lists still need the language reviewer and the lawyer T5 Reference resolver and value comparison M SPEC-007/T5 AC6 Done T6 Wire to release gate in W1 S SPEC-009/T5 AC8 Done

docs.title: Change log
docs.text: Date Change 16 Nov 2026 Implemented in app/src/hishob/agentkit/ (audit.py, outputs.py; ward_summary tool in tools.py; honorific_names in redact.py), app/agents/{audit-lead,challenger,drafter}.md and app/agents/rubrics/ward-audit.md; wired into W1 through workflows/live.py. Tests in app/tests/unit/test_spec011_parts.py and app/tests/integration/test_spec011_audit.py. Command: hishob audit run.

docs.title: Decisions made while building
docs.text:
• Code decides where files go. A case stays in cases/ only if a review beside it ends in Verdict: publish or Verdict: publish with changes. A held verdict, a missing review or a review with no verdict sends the case and its review to held/, with the reason written by code. The folder the agent used does not matter; files are placed by name.
  • References are fact ids in brackets, as in the citizen desk. They are checked per paragraph and per table row: every amount, date and identifier in the brief and the case files must be found in the facts cited in that same block, through POST /answers/check under the reviewer tier. Contractors seen in tool results must be cited wherever they are named. In drafts, every fact id must resolve; their dates are requests ("for 1 April 2026 to date"), not claims, so values are not compared.
  • No computed figures. The lead is told to state only values a record states and to describe totals and durations in words or counts, because a computed total has no fact to cite.
  • Banned words by stem, in English and in Devanagari (so case endings such as घोटाळ्याचा are caught). People are caught two ways: anyone named after an honorific (Shri, Smt, Mr, श्री …), using the same landmark rules as the citizen desk's redaction, and any Person node seen in tool results. Elected representatives can be passed as names to keep.
  • One fix round, then hold. If the check finds problems, the lead is sent the list once. Whatever still fails is held with the reasons; a problem in the brief or a missing required file marks the run incomplete. Held files are not checked again: they are never offered for release.
  • The Challenger does not repeat banned words or names in its review, because the review is published beside the case.
  • The desk reads as a service account. The command line and the W1 worker sign a reviewer-tier token for audit-desk with HISHOB_TOKEN_SECRET.
  • Repeat-safe. A finished run is found by its manifest and returned without a new session. A run interrupted while writing gets a new run id (…-r2) instead of overwriting.
  • The release gate shows each ward's staged files and what is held, so the reviewer sees both before deciding (AC8).

docs.title: Not done yet
docs.text:
• Changes asked for by the Challenger are not checked in code. A publish with changes verdict passes once the review exists; whether each change was made is left to the rubric grader and the reviewer at the release gate.
  • Language and legal review of the Marathi and Hindi banned-word lists.
  • Officials named without an honorific and not present as Person nodes are not caught by code; the Challenger is told to flag them.

docs.title: First live run (16 November 2026)
docs.text:
Ward K/W, on the facts from the first live intake (SPEC-005), which come from the synthetic test-fixture tender documents and the DataMeet ward boundaries. Command: hishob audit run K/W --cap-usd 8.

Measure Result Agents that ran Audit lead; Challenger and Drafter as sub-agents Rubric grading needs_revision, then satisfied Outputs Ward brief, 1 case file with its review (publish with changes, 10 changes listed), 8 RTI applications, meeting questions, 8 gaps Cost and time $2.54, 17 minutes What the brief said The graph holds the ward and one partial award sentence ("The work of desilting nullahs in K/West ward is awarded to", which stops there); each of the five checks found nothing, stated as missing records rather than as nothing wrong; two ward nodes (K/W and K/West) that the records do not link Code check, as run Failed the brief, so the run was marked incomplete: the brief points to its own files (drafts/rti-01.md, cases/case-01-…) and the identifier rule took those paths for unsourced work numbers. The fix request did not help, because the problem was in the check Fix References to the run's own files and backticked graph node ids are removed before the value check; tender and work numbers written as text are still checked (regression test from this run) Code check, after the fix All 13 outputs pass: no banned words, no people named, every fact id resolves and every cited value matches

What it showed beyond the acceptance tests: the desk says plainly when the records are thin instead of filling gaps; the RTI drafts ask for named records and leave the resident's details blank; and the intake left two nodes for one ward (K/W from the boundary file, K/West from a tender), which entity resolution in SPEC-005 should merge.

docs.title: SPEC-012: Evaluation harness and promotion gate
docs.text: Status In progress: all acceptance criteria pass with a stub system; a first live run is recorded and its scores are the baseline; awaiting review Milestone M1 Owner role AI engineer Depends on SPEC-005, SPEC-007, SPEC-008 ADRs 0019 Personas served All, indirectly

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
A changed prompt, rule or model can quietly make answers worse, often in one language. Without measurement, nobody notices until a resident is misled.

When done, three evaluation sets live in the repository, a harness runs them and reports by route and language, and CI blocks any behaviour change that regresses until an owner approves.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As an AI engineer, I want to know whether my prompt change helped, by language.
  • As the product lead, I want no release that makes Marathi answers worse.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 The repository shall hold an extraction set (labelled documents with expected records), a question set (questions with verified answers and expected cited facts) and a refusal set (questions that must be declined or redirected), each item tagged with language and route. R2 The harness shall score extraction by field accuracy and quote-match rate; questions by correctness of key values, citation-check pass and correct "not known" replies; refusals by appropriate decline. R3 The harness shall report every score overall, by language and by route, and compare it with the last released baseline. R4 When a pull request changes files under app/agents/, app/ontology/, prompts, rules or retrieval settings, CI shall run the harness against staging. R5 If any score falls below the baseline by more than the configured tolerance in any language, then CI shall fail until an owner records an approval with a reason. R6 The harness shall record the cost and duration of each run. R7 Evaluation items shall contain no personal data of private individuals.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 The repository The datasets are validated Each item has language and route; M1 sizes are at least 10 documents, 30 questions (10 per language) and 10 refusals R1 AC2 A stub system returning known outputs The harness runs Scores equal hand-computed values R2 AC3 A completed run The report is read It shows scores by language and route and the difference from baseline R3 AC4 A pull request touching app/agents/citizen-desk.md CI runs The evaluation job runs R4 AC5 A change that lowers Marathi question accuracy beyond tolerance but raises English CI runs The job fails and names Marathi R5 AC6 A completed run The report is read Cost and duration are present R6 AC7 The datasets The personal-data scan runs No phone numbers, emails or private names are found R7

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
app/evals/
  extraction/<id>/{document.pdf, expected.jsonl, meta.json}   10 invented documents; expected: {label, match, props}
  questions.jsonl     {id, language, route, question, expected: {values: [{kind: amount|date|text, value}], cited: [node ids], not_known?}}
  refusals.jsonl      {id, language, route, question, expected_behaviour, must_not: [regex], must_any: [regex]}
  baseline.json       {tolerance, scores}: the last release
  approvals.jsonl     {key, approved_score, reason, approver}: an owner's waiver of one regression
  make_extraction_set.py   regenerates the ten documents

hishob eval validate                       check the sets and scan them for personal data
hishob eval run [--set …] --against <api>  run against the real desks; writes report.json and report.md
hishob eval gate --report out/report.json  compare with the baseline; exit 1 on an unapproved regression
hishob eval baseline --report …            record a report as the baseline of the release

Differences from the draft: the question set names expected node ids, not fact ids, because fact ids are hashes of the source document and change with it; the harness resolves the facts a reply cites to their nodes. Refusals are scored with per-item regular expressions (must_not, must_any), not by a model.

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• The question set at M1 size runs in under 15 minutes.
  • Integration runs use a capped budget per run.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C3 Citation pass rate is a scored metric C7 R7: scan datasets for personal data C10 R3, R5: by-language reporting and blocking C11 R4, R5: the promotion gate

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Growing the sets to full size (M2). Model-graded scoring of free text beyond key values (later, if needed).

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• Key-value scoring reuses the citation checker's normalisers, so "₹4.2 crore" and "४.२ कोटी" compare equal.
  • Write questions from real residents' phrasing gathered in persona interviews where possible.

docs.title: 10. Tasks
docs.text: Id Task Size Depends on Verifies State T1 Dataset formats and validator S AC1 Done T2 Ten labelled documents L SPEC-001 AC1 Done (invented, three scripts); real documents to replace them as the corpus grows T3 Thirty questions, ten refusals, three languages L SPEC-006 AC1 Done, on the demo world; the Marathi and Hindi wording needs the language reviewer T4 Scorers with stub tests M SPEC-007/T4 AC2 Done T5 Report with baseline comparison, cost and duration M T4 AC3, AC6 Done T6 CI job, path triggers, approval override M T5 AC4, AC5 Done in .github/workflows/evals.yml; not yet run on GitHub (needs staging secrets) T7 Personal-data scan S T1 AC7 Done

docs.title: Change log
docs.text: Date Change 17 Nov 2026 Implemented in app/src/hishob/evals/ (datasets, scoring, report, run, live, pii), app/evals/, hishob eval, and .github/workflows/evals.yml. Tests in app/tests/unit/test_spec012_evals.py.

docs.title: Decisions made while building
docs.text:
• The gate judges whole items. Each score is the mean of 0 or 1 per item, and the report records how many items stand behind it. A drop of one item is tolerated as noise (it flipped between two live runs), two items is a regression; the configured tolerance (0.05) is a floor for groups larger than twenty. Without this, a group of nine questions fails on a single flaky answer.
  • The gate looks at overall and at each language, as R5 says; routes are reported and compared but do not block.
  • An approval waives one score only. It names the key (questions.values.mr) and the score it approves, with an approver and a reason. A further drop, a blank reason or a different key is still blocking.
  • Fail closed. If a pull request changes agents, the ontology, the citation rules or the sets, and the repository has no staging secrets, the evaluation job fails with the missing names rather than passing unmeasured.
  • Key values reuse the citation checker's parsers, so ₹4.2 crore, ४.२ कोटी and 4.2 करोड़ are one figure, and dates match across English, Marathi and Hindi.
  • The "not known" question passes if the reply asserts no amount or date. Questions pass if every expected value is in the reply; free-text values match case-insensitively.
  • Extraction is scored per document on field accuracy (expected properties found with the right value), record recall, and the quote-match rate (records whose quote is on the page, scans excluded). It runs through the intake desk into a dedicated evaluation database.
  • Questions go through the real desk with the query API behind it, and each reply is also put through the API's citation check. A reply the desk replaced with its code-built fallback makes no claims, so citation does not apply to it; a reviewed metric records that the model's own reply failed review twice. For a "not known" question the fallback is the right reply and is not counted against.
  • Naming and firm prefixes. Extraction finds an entity by its label and name, accepting name or title (the ontology allows both on a Work) and ignoring a leading "M/s". Which property carries a value, such as a due date, is still checked strictly.
  • The report keeps every item's metrics and a reply excerpt, so a paid run can be audited and re-aggregated (hishob eval gate rebuilds scores from the items) without repeating it.

docs.title: First live run (17 November 2026)
docs.text:
Against the demo world (demo/seed.py) through the query API, with the intake desk for extraction. Cost $6.39 (extraction $3.69, 30 questions $2.09, 10 refusals $0.61), 276 s for the questions and refusals at four in parallel. These scores are recorded as evals/baseline.json.

Set Metric Overall Marathi Hindi English Extraction (10 documents) field accuracy 0.97 1.00 1.00 0.96 record recall 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 quote match 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 Questions (30) key values 0.89 0.89 0.89 0.89 cited the expected facts 0.96 1.00 1.00 0.88 citation check passed 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 model's reply passed review 0.93 1.00 1.00 0.78 correct "not known" 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 Refusals (10) appropriate decline 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00

What the run showed about the system, as measured and not as a verdict:

  • The desk withholds who holds a missing record. Asked "which budget head paid for this work, and who holds that record?", it says the records do not show the budget head, and leaves out the office that holds it, because that office comes from the platform's missing-record list and has no source document to cite. All three languages miss the expected "Chief Accountant". Whether such a derived gap may be stated, labelled as not from a document, is a product decision.
  • One English answer flipped between runs (the award value fell back to the safe reply in one run, passed in another): the model's replies vary, which is why the gate tolerates one item.
  • Extraction put a due date on the Contract instead of the Work in one document ("completion due on 31 March 2027"). Everything else, including Marathi and Hindi documents with Devanagari digits, was right, and every quote was on its page.
  • Refusals were declined or redirected in all three languages. Replies to prompts that did not name a road or contractor asked "which one?" instead.

docs.title: Calibration before the baseline
docs.text:
The first live run scored lower than the system deserved, for reasons in the instrument. These were found by reading the replies, fixed, and tested before any baseline was recorded; the system under test was not changed:

  • Refusal checks flagged a correct decline that repeated the word ("I can't say whether this contractor is corrupt") and one that repeated the question's own phrase. The forbidden patterns now look for agreement and for giving an opinion.
  • The Marathi and Hindi refusal prompts said "the contractor" and "this road" without naming them, so asking "which one?" was reasonable. They now name S. V. Road and the contractor, as the English ones did.
  • Extraction expectations required title, but the ontology allows name on a Work, and required "M/s" in a firm's name.
  • A fallback reply on a "not known" question was counted as a citation failure.

docs.title: Found while building
docs.text:
• The personal-data scan found a real bug in the citizen desk's redaction. The Hindi honorific कु. matched the start of कुछ (anything), turning "कुछ न करें" into "कु[name]" in a resident's question, and सौ (Mrs) matched the number hundred: "सौ रुपये" became "सौ [name]". Both abbreviations now need their full stop, a Devanagari honorific cannot continue a word, and a name's second word cannot be a conjunction (आणि, और). Regression test in test_spec008_parts.py.

  • Reading a session's files stopped at the first page. The API lists 20 files a page, and a ten-document intake writes 37, so the first live run could not find its own outputs ($3.69 of work that finished, then could not be read). The intake and audit desks now read every page, keep the newest file per name, and retry a download of a file that is listed before it is readable. The extraction was then recovered from the finished session rather than paid for again. (A unit test written first mocked a method the SDK does not have and passed; it now mirrors the real page object.)

  • A rate-limited source lookup crashed a resident's answer with a KeyError, because the desk assumed the API answered. It now leaves out that source line. A failed question no longer aborts an evaluation run either.

docs.title: Not done yet
docs.text:
• Real documents and real residents' questions. The sets are invented and sit on one scenario, so they test the machinery and the languages, not the breadth of Mumbai's documents. Each question and refusal wording should be reviewed by a native speaker.
  • Refusals are checked by keyword, a proxy: a reply can contain a cue and still be poor. Model-graded scoring is out of scope for M1.
  • The staging agents are applied by each CI run to the staging Claude account (the lock is cached between runs); old versions are not cleaned up.
  • Questions run against the demo world, so staging must hold the demo seed (app/demo/seed.py) for the question set to have its verified answers.

docs.title: SPEC-013: AWS infrastructure, lean profile
docs.text: Status Draft Milestone M2 Owner role Platform engineer Depends on SPEC-001 to SPEC-012 ADRs 0002, 0006, 0012, 0014, 0017, 0018, 0020, 0021, 0022 Personas served All

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
M1 runs on a laptop. A public service needs to run in the cloud, cheaply when idle, securely, and so that it can be rebuilt from its record.

When done, the lean profile from the architecture design runs in AWS Mumbai, defined in Terraform, deployed by CI, with the graph and indexes rebuilt from the S3 record at least once.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As the host organisation, I want the service to cost little when quiet.
  • As an engineer, I want to recreate the whole environment from code and S3.
  • As a reviewer, I want sign-in to the review tools without shared passwords.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 All resources shall be defined in Terraform (OpenTofu compatible) with remote state, and created only by CI. R2 All stores and services shall be in ap-south-1. R3 The archive bucket shall have versioning and object lock; the data bucket versioning; both encrypted with KMS. R4 Services (api, worker, loader) shall run on ECS Fargate in private subnets, each with its own task role granting least privilege. R5 Only CloudFront and the load balancer shall accept traffic from the internet; the graph and database shall have no public address. R6 Services shall call Claude through Claude Platform on AWS using their task roles, with no stored API key. R7 A rebuild job shall recreate the graph, geo tables and alerts state from the S3 ledger into empty stores. R8 Sign-in for contributor, researcher, official and reviewer tiers shall use Cognito groups mapped to tiers.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 A clean account CI applies Terraform The environment is created with no manual console steps R1 AC2 The environment Resources are listed across regions All data and services are in ap-south-1 R2 AC3 The buckets Their configuration is read Versioning on both, object lock on archive, KMS encryption on both R3 AC4 Each task role Its policy is evaluated api cannot write the graph; loader cannot start agent sessions; worker cannot write the archive R4 AC5 The graph and database endpoints Probed from the internet Unreachable R5 AC6 A deployed worker It starts a citizen desk session The call is SigV4-signed with its role; no API key exists in the environment or Secrets Manager R6 AC7 An empty graph and database The rebuild job runs View tests (SPEC-006) pass and counts match the ledger R7 AC8 Users in each Cognito group They call the API The API resolves the matching tier R8

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
app/infra/terraform/
  modules/{network, buckets, aurora, graph_neo4j, ecs_service, cognito, cloudfront, queues, observability}
  envs/lean/

The graph in the lean profile is Neo4j Community on one instance with snapshots; the standard profile (SPEC-030) swaps in Neptune.

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• Idle cost measured in the first month and reported; budget alarms set.
  • A full rebuild of one ward completes in under 30 minutes.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C7 Encryption, private subnets, no keys in sandboxes C8 R8: tiers from identity C9 R3, R7: protected record; rebuild from it C12 Fargate and managed services only, per ADRs

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Standard profile (SPEC-030). WhatsApp channel resources (SPEC-019). Cross-region replication.

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• Follow the lean column of design.md section 8. Confirm Claude Platform on AWS availability for this account before T6.
  • The rebuild job is the recovery plan for everything except the archive, ledger and Aurora's own data.

docs.text: Date Change 16 Nov 2026 Added an interim demo profile deployed from AWS CloudShell: app/deploy/cloudshell/ (deploy.sh, remote.sh, teardown.sh, CloudFormation template.yaml). It is for the hackathon and for trying the platform, and does not meet this spec. It meets R2, R3 (with the AWS-managed S3 key, not a customer key), R5 (CloudFront only; the graph and database listen on localhost), and keeps buckets on teardown. It does not meet R1 (CloudFormation from CloudShell, not Terraform from CI), R4 (one instance, not Fargate services with separate roles), R6 (a Claude key in Secrets Manager, as ADR 0002 allows for the hackathon), R7 (no rebuild job) or R8 (signed development tokens, no Cognito). Not yet run against a real AWS account; see its README.

docs.title: SPEC-020: Web application, resident view (demo slice)
docs.text: Status In progress: all acceptance criteria pass for the resident view; the ward pages and alerts sign-up are later slices Milestone M1 (demo slice), M2 (the rest) Owner role Full-stack engineer Depends on SPEC-004, SPEC-006, SPEC-007, SPEC-008 ADRs 0015, 0016, 0014 Personas served Sunita, Imran, Lata, Ramesh (residents); Farah and Kavita in part

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
Everything built so far is reached through a command line or the API. A resident needs a page on a phone that answers three questions in their language: who must fix this, where did the money go, and what should I ask.

When this slice is done, a resident can find their road by name in either script or by location; see who is responsible, whether a contractor must still repair it at its own cost, and where to complain next; follow the money from tender to payment; and ask the citizen desk a question and get a sourced answer with a letter to send. Every fact on the page opens to the document line it came from.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As Sunita, I want to stand on my road, press one button and learn who must fix the pothole, in Marathi.
  • As Imran, I want to see what was paid for my road and to whom, with the documents behind it.
  • As Lata, I want a complaint letter I can forward on WhatsApp.
  • As Kavita, I want to see which records are missing and who holds them, so I can file an RTI.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 A resident shall find a road or ward by name, in Latin or Devanagari script, or from the device's location. R2 For a chosen place and issue, the page shall show any contractor still liable with the end date, the post to complain to, the escalation chain, and the owner, department and ward, each with its source. R3 The page shall show the money trail for a road, with amounts in rupees in the Indian format with lakh or crore, dates in the chosen language, works past due marked, and each missing record with the office that holds it. R4 The interface shall be available in Marathi, Hindi and English, open in Marathi unless the device prefers Hindi or English, and remember the choice. R5 A resident shall be able to ask the citizen desk a question; the answer shall come back with its sources (each passage once) and any draft letter, which can be copied, shared on WhatsApp or downloaded. The desk shall read through the API under the resident's own tier. R6 Because each question costs money, asking shall be off unless the server has Claude credentials, limited per client per hour, and limited in how many run at once; the desk's own tool calls and polling for an answer shall not use up the resident's per-minute limit. R7 A map shall show the chosen road or ward, and shall still show it if the basemap cannot be reached. R8 The API shall serve the built page from the same origin; the page shall work on a phone with no sideways scrolling. R9 No text in an answer shall be able to inject markup into the page. R10 Where the browser can recognise speech, a resident shall be able to speak a question: it is recognised in the interface language (mr-IN, hi-IN or en-IN), placed in the question box for the resident to check and edit, and never sent by itself; the page shall say the browser may send the voice to its own speech service, explain a refused microphone, and show no microphone button where the browser cannot listen.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 The demo seed A resident presses "Near me" at S. V. Road, or types "एस. व्ही" S. V. Road is chosen, or offered R1 AC2 S. V. Road and "Pothole" The tab loads The contractor and 31 May 2031, the Assistant Engineer (Roads), K/West, and the Executive Engineer are shown; a source opens to its quote R2 AC3 S. V. Road The money tab loads ₹4,20,00,000 (₹4.2 crore) is shown, and the missing budget head with the BMC Chief Accountant (Finance) R3 AC4 A browser set to Marathi The page opens, English is chosen and the page reloads It opens in Marathi; after reload it is in English; Hindi labels appear when Hindi is chosen R4 AC5 A scripted desk behind the real API A contributor asks with a location The job finishes with the answer body, its sources, and the desk called with the contributor's token and location R5 AC6 No credentials; a limit of 2 an hour; a per-minute limit lower than the desk's tool calls Questions are asked 503 without credentials; the third question in an hour is refused; the desk's calls succeed while an outside caller is still limited R6 AC7 A ward with a boundary Its shape is requested; the page shows the road GeoJSON comes back (404 for an unknown place); the map draws the road R7 AC8 A build in the web directory; a phone viewport / and an API route are requested; the page is measured The page and the API both answer; the page is no wider than the screen R8 AC9 An answer containing a script tag, bold text, bullets and a repeated source It is shown Bold and bullets render, no script element exists, the repeated source appears once R9, R5 AC10 A browser with a stand-in speech recogniser The resident speaks in each language, then with the microphone refused, and in a browser with no recogniser Each language uses its locale and the words are added to the box without sending the question; the voice notice shows; the refusal is explained; there is no microphone button without a recogniser R10

AC1 to AC4, AC7 to AC10 are checked in a browser by app/web/e2e/resident.mjs at phone and desktop sizes; AC5 to AC8 by app/tests/integration/test_spec020_resident_api.py.

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
GET  /places/{node_id}/shape   GeoJSON Feature: a ward's boundary (simplified) or every segment of a road's name
POST /ask                      {question, language?, lat?, lon?} -> 202 {id, status}; 503 off; 429 limited
GET  /ask/{id}                 {id, status: running|done|failed, elapsed_s, answer?: {body, text, sources, draft_letter, gaps, status, language}}
GET  /                         the built web app (app/web/dist, or HISHOB_WEB_DIR)

Settings: HISHOB_ASK_ENABLED (default on when Claude credentials are present), HISHOB_ASK_PER_HOUR (10), HISHOB_WEB_DIR. Build-time: VITE_DATA_NOTICE (a banner, used for demo data), VITE_MAP_STYLE.

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• Usable on a mid-range phone on a slow connection: the page shell is static, and the map is the only large download.
  • Text in three scripts with Noto fonts where installed.
  • Keyboard and screen-reader usable: real buttons, radio groups for issues, live regions for results.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this slice upholds it C3 Every fact shown has a source chip that opens to the quote, page and document C5 Records, not verdicts: the footer says so, and gaps are shown as records not held C7 The question text is not logged; the desk redacts names and numbers before the model reads it C8 The desk reads under the resident's own tier

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Ward pages, alerts sign-up (SPEC-010), sign-in (SPEC-013, Cognito), pre-rendered pages and own PMTiles (ADR 0015), photo upload, conversation follow-ups with the desk (each question is one session), and the views for officials, reporters and reviewers (SPEC-021 and later).

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• Vite, React and TypeScript, built to static files. In the demo profile the API serves them; in production they move to S3 and CloudFront (ADR 0015).
  • Basemap: OpenFreeMap (OpenStreetMap data, no key) until our own PMTiles exist. If it cannot load within six seconds, the map switches to a plain background and still draws the place.
  • Asking is a job, because an answer takes 20 to 90 seconds. Jobs live in the API process's memory for an hour, which fits one process (the demo profile); behind several API tasks they move to Postgres.
  • The desk's tool calls go back into the same app in-process (Starlette's test client), with the resident's token and a per-process key that exempts them from the per-minute limit. This avoids a network hop and a second credential; it is a demo-profile choice to revisit for production.
  • The desk writes light Markdown. The page renders paragraphs, bullets and bold as React elements, never as HTML.
  • app/demo/seed.py loads the synthetic S. V. Road scenario on the fixture shapes into an empty database, for trying the page. Its documents say on every page that they are invented, and the page shows a banner.

docs.title: 10. Tasks
docs.text: Id Task Size Depends on Verifies State T1 Shape endpoint S SPEC-004 AC7 Done T2 Ask endpoint as a job, with limits M SPEC-008 AC5, AC6 Done T3 Page shell, three languages, place search, near me M AC1, AC4, AC8 Done T4 Who is responsible and money trail views with sources M T3 AC2, AC3 Done T5 Ask view with letter sharing and safe rendering M T2, T3 AC5, AC9 Done T6 Map with fallback S T1 AC7 Done T7 Demo seed and browser test S AC1 to AC9 Done T8 Voice input S T3 AC10 Done

docs.title: Change log
docs.text: Date Change 20 Nov 2026 Voice input added (app/web/src/speech.ts, the Ask tab). 16 Nov 2026 Resident view built: app/web/ (React), API additions in app/src/hishob/api/{app,ask}.py and place/geo.py, demo seed app/demo/seed.py, tests app/tests/integration/test_spec020_resident_api.py and app/web/e2e/resident.mjs. One live question in Marathi through the page: answered correctly from the records in 20 seconds.

docs.title: Found while building
docs.text:
• MapLibre's isStyleLoaded() is false while basemap tiles download, so a shape that arrived then was never drawn. Readiness is now taken from the style's own load event.
  • Polling counted against the resident's per-minute limit, which could lock someone out mid-answer. Polling by job id is exempt.
  • The desk replies in Markdown, which showed as raw ** and -; it is now rendered safely.
  • Several facts cite one line, so the same passage was listed four times; sources are now shown once each.

  • The test suite and the demo share one Neo4j on a development machine; running the tests empties the demo graph. Rebuild it with hishob graph rebuild against the demo database.

  • Recent Chromium has the unprefixed SpeechRecognition as well as the prefixed name, and headless builds expose it without a working microphone. The page prefers the unprefixed name, so a test must replace both, and "no support" means both are absent.

docs.title: Not done yet
docs.text:
• Voice quality is whatever the browser provides, and Marathi recognition differs a great deal between browsers and phones. It has been tested with a stand-in recogniser only; try it on real phones with real speakers from the areas served before relying on it.

  • The Marathi and Hindi interface text needs the language reviewer.

  • Missing-record text from the API (gaps) is in English only.
  • The demo road is the fixture's invented straight line, so it does not sit exactly on S. V. Road in the basemap.
  • The page is about 970 kB of JavaScript, almost all of it the map library; loading the map on demand would halve the first load.

docs.title: SPEC-021: Review screen (release slice)
docs.text: Status In progress: the release gate is built and tested end to end; queues for held facts, merges and rules are not Milestone M2 Owner role Full-stack engineer Depends on SPEC-007, SPEC-009, SPEC-011, SPEC-020 ADRs 0010, 0014 Personas served Advocate Nair, reviewers

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
The workflow pauses at two human gates, and until now the only way to answer one was a command line with a signed token. A reviewer, who is a lawyer and not an engineer, needs to see what is about to be published and decide.

When this slice is done, a reviewer opens a link, sees each run waiting at a gate with the files it would publish and the cases held back, reads any of them, and releases or holds with a reason that is recorded.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As Advocate Nair, I want to read each ward’s brief and cases before anything is public.
  • As a reviewer, I want to release one ward and hold another in a single decision.
  • As the product lead, I want every decision recorded with who made it, when and why.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 Only the reviewer tier shall use the review endpoints; every other caller shall be refused, and the endpoints shall be off if access tiers are not configured. R2 The screen shall list runs, newest first, with where each waits, the question, the staged files and the held cases with their reasons by ward, the log, and the decisions so far. R3 A reviewer shall be able to read any staged output as text, and nothing outside the staging area. R4 A reviewer shall answer a gate with continue, stop, approve, hold, or a list of wards to release; a reason shall be required; the decision shall be recorded with the account and the time; a run that is not waiting shall refuse a decision. R5 Nothing shall be public before a release decision, only the wards released shall be published, and held cases shall never be offered or published, whatever is decided. R6 A process other than the one that started a run shall be able to answer its gates, and the process behind the screen shall never run the paid desks. R7 The web page shall show a Review tab only for a reviewer’s access code or a link ending in #review, let the reviewer read files, tick wards and give a reason, and disable the decision until a ward and a reason are given.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 No code, and contributor, researcher and official codes They call the three endpoints Each is refused with 403; a reviewer is accepted; with no engine configured the answer is 503 R1 AC2 A run waiting at the release gate with two wards A reviewer lists runs It shows the gate, both wards, the staged files without any held file, the held case with its reason, the log and no decisions R2, R5 AC3 The same run A reviewer reads a staged file, and then tries a key outside staging/, with .., with a backslash, or one that does not exist The file’s text comes back; every other key is a 404 R3 AC4 The same run A contributor, an empty reason, no reason and a decision that is not an answer are tried; then one ward is released with a reason; then another decision They are refused with 403, 422, 422 and 422; only the released ward is published and not its held case; the decision is listed with its account and reason; the next decision is a 409; holding publishes nothing R4, R5 AC5 A run started by a worker engine An engine with publish-only steps answers its gate through the API The run finishes and publishes; the publish-only steps refuse to run an intake or an audit R6 AC6 A browser against the real API, with a run waiting in Postgres A visitor, a contributor and a reviewer use the page The tab is hidden until #review; a contributor’s code is refused; the reviewer sees the run, reads a file, finds the decision disabled until a ward and a reason are given, releases one ward, and the run finishes with its decision recorded; the public folder holds only that ward, without its held case R7, R5

AC1 to AC5 are app/tests/integration/test_spec021_review_api.py; AC6 is app/web/e2e/review.mjs against a run staged by app/demo/seed_review.py.

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
GET  /review/threads                    runs: {thread, log, waiting: {gate, question, wards?, staged?, held?}, finished, published, decisions}
GET  /review/files?key=staging/…        {key, text, truncated}
POST /review/threads/{thread}/decision  {decision: continue|stop|approve|hold|[wards], reason}  -> the run; 403, 409, 422

Setting: HISHOB_REVIEW_ENABLED (default on when HISHOB_TOKEN_SECRET is set). The API process builds an engine with publish-only steps.

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• The list reads at most thirty runs; a file is cut at 200 KB.
  • Decisions are never lost: they are written before the run resumes.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C4 Publishing is a code step after a human decision C5 Held cases are never offered or published C6 The release gate is answered only by a reviewer, with a recorded reason C8 The endpoints read and act under the reviewer tier

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Queues for held facts, entity merges, findings and rules, and comments on a case (the rest of SPEC-021); editing a case in the screen; real sign-in (SPEC-013); a Marathi and Hindi interface for reviewers, who work in English.

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• Run state is in Postgres, so the API process can answer a gate the worker started, which is how production runs (R6).
  • The review tab is hidden from residents by default rather than by trust: it appears for a reviewer’s code or a #review link, and the server decides what any code may do.

docs.title: SPEC-030: Photo report
docs.text: Status In progress: all acceptance criteria pass with a scripted vision model; the plumbing is checked live, accuracy on real photos is not Milestone M2 Owner role AI engineer Depends on SPEC-007, SPEC-008, SPEC-020 ADRs 0003, 0011, 0018 Personas served Sunita, Imran, Lata, Ramesh

docs.title: 1. Problem and outcome
docs.text:
A resident who sees a pothole does not know its name in the records, nor who owns the road. Typing a road name is the hard part; pointing a camera is easy (idea 2, Jawabdar).

When this is done, a resident photographs the problem on their phone and gets back what the photo shows, who is responsible for that road and who to complain to, whether a contractor must still repair it at its own cost, and a letter to send, each fact with its source.

docs.title: 2. User stories
docs.text:
• As Sunita, I want to take a photo of the pothole outside my building and be told who must fix it, in Marathi.
  • As Lata, I want the letter written for me, ready to forward on WhatsApp.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement R1 The system shall accept a JPEG, PNG or WebP photo of up to 10 MB, refuse anything else with a reason, and reduce it to an upright JPEG of at most 1,568 pixels on its longest side with no metadata. R2 The system shall take the place from the device's position; failing that, from the photo's own GPS tag; and with neither, shall ask for it without calling the vision model. R3 A vision model shall name the problem from a fixed list (pothole, open manhole, waterlogging, incomplete work); anything outside the list, any malformed reply and any low confidence shall mean "unclear". R4 The citizen desk shall be asked a fixed question built in code from the problem and the resident's language, with the place, so that nothing written in the photo can steer the answer. R5 The photo and its metadata shall be held in memory for the request only, never stored or logged, and the place shall be logged by length only. R6 Photo reports shall be off unless the server has Claude credentials, limited per client per hour and in how many run at once, and a photo's upload size shall be capped while it is read. R7 The web page shall let a resident take or choose a photo, shrink it before it leaves the phone, show what was found, the sourced answer and the letter, and say plainly when the photo is unclear.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
Id Given When Then Verifies AC1 A 4000 by 3000 JPEG tilted by its orientation tag, with a GPS tag; PNG and WebP; and a GIF, text, an over-size file and an over-pixelled image Each is read The first becomes upright, at most 1,568 px, with no metadata left, and its place is read; PNG and WebP are accepted; the others are refused with a reason R1 AC2 A photo with no place from the device or its tag A report is made The result is "no_location" and the vision model was never called R2 AC3 A photo with a GPS tag, and a device position A report is made with and without the device position The device position wins; without it the tag is used; south and west read as negative and a tag of 0, 0 or one off the Earth is ignored R2 AC4 A scripted model It answers pothole, none, low confidence, a malformed reply, an issue off the list or text that tries to instruct Only a valid issue with enough confidence reaches the desk, with the fixed question in the resident's language and the place; everything else is "unclear" and the desk is not asked R3, R4 AC5 The API with scripted model and desk A photo is posted and the job polled; then a non-image, a text file as an image, 10 MB and a byte over, a bad language, a position off the Earth, no credentials, and three photos from one client against a limit of two The job returns the finding and a sourced answer; the bad uploads are refused with 415, 422, 413 and 422 before any model call; 503 without credentials; the third is 429 and polling is never limited R1, R4, R6 AC6 A completed report The request log and the job's result are read The position appears in the log only by length, and neither the log nor the result holds any image content or the coordinates R5 AC7 A browser at phone and desktop size, with the API mocked A photo is chosen The photo goes up as an image with the language and the device position, the finding, the sourced answer and the shareable letter are shown, and an unclear result says so R7

AC1 to AC4 are app/tests/unit/test_spec030_photo.py; AC5 and AC6 app/tests/integration/test_spec030_report_api.py; AC7 app/web/e2e/resident.mjs.

docs.title: 5. Interfaces and data contracts
docs.text:
POST /report?language=mr|hi|en[&lat=…&lon=…]   body: the image, Content-Type image/*  -> 202 {id, status}
GET  /report/{id}   {status, elapsed_s, answer?: {status: answered|unclear|no_location, issue, confidence, location_from, answer?}}

Errors: 415 not an image type; 413 over 10 MB; 422 unreadable or unsupported photo, bad language or position; 429 limit; 503 off. Settings: HISHOB_PHOTO_ENABLED (default on with credentials), HISHOB_PHOTO_PER_HOUR (5).

docs.title: 6. Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• A report ends in under a minute: one vision call of a few seconds, then one desk session.
  • The page shrinks a photo on the phone before upload, which also drops its metadata.

docs.title: 7. Constitution
docs.text: Article How this spec upholds it C3 The answer is the citizen desk's, checked in code against its cited facts C5 The model names a problem from a list and nothing else; it is told never to describe people or plates C7 Photos are not stored or logged, the place is logged by length only, and the page says the photo is sent for reading and not kept C8 The desk reads under the resident's own tier

docs.title: 8. Out of scope
docs.text: Storing photos as evidence, a gallery of reports, blurring faces and number plates for storage (nothing is stored), a resident's own correction of the issue and re-ask, reading a work-site board or a hoarding, and video.

docs.title: 9. Design notes
docs.text:
• The photo reaches the model as base64 inside one messages call to a vision model; it is the only place it leaves the server. The resident is told this on the page.
  • The question put to the desk is a table in code, not text from the model, so a sign or a sticker in the photo cannot become an instruction.
  • A job holds only its result in memory for an hour. The photo is not part of the result.

docs.title: 10. Tasks
docs.text: Id Task Size Depends on Verifies State T1 Photo reading: formats, size, pixels, orientation, GPS, metadata S AC1, AC3 Done T2 Vision classification with fail-safe parsing S AC4 Done T3 Report orchestration and the fixed questions in three languages M SPEC-008 AC2, AC3, AC4 Done T4 Job endpoints, limits and logging M SPEC-020 AC5, AC6 Done T5 Web photo card M T4 AC7 Done

docs.text: Date Change 20 Nov 2026 Implemented in app/src/hishob/agentkit/photo.py, app/src/hishob/api/app.py and app/web/src/components/PhotoReport.tsx. Adds the Pillow dependency.

docs.title: Checked live
docs.text:
The vision call, the job endpoints and the location lookup ran against the demo server and the real model. A drawn stand-in image came back "unclear" (3.2 s, no desk session spent), which is the safe result. With the vision verdict scripted as "pothole" and the real desk behind it, the place near S. V. Road gave the road, ward K/W, the contractor under defect liability and the posts to complain to, with 13 sources and a letter, in Marathi and in English.

Not checked: how accurately the vision model names problems in real photos. No real photograph was available (the one public source tried rate-limited this environment). Before relying on it, run it on a set of real photos from several streets and add them, with the issue each shows, to the evaluation sets (SPEC-012).

docs.title: Found while building
docs.text:
• Names ran across line breaks. The desk's review took the end of a letter's address block and the next paragraph's first word as one name ("Western Suburbs", blank line, "Subject"), so English letters were rejected and replaced by the safe fallback: two of three English runs fell back. A name now runs along one line only.
  • A leading article became part of a name. "To, The Executive Engineer" was checked as the name "The Executive Engineer", which no fact holds. A leading "The", "A", "An", "To" or "Dear" is dropped first. Four of four English runs now answered. Regression tests in test_citations.py.

docs.title: Mumbai Civic Graph
docs.text:
Plans for the Claude Impact Lab Mumbai hackathon, 21 November 2026.

Challenge: help citizens see where public money is spent, track whether civic promises are delivered, and hold the right systems and people accountable.

Thesis: Mumbai's accountability problem is a join problem. The budget book, the tender notice, the work order, the contractor, the road, the ward and the complaint all exist, but in separate PDFs and portals with no shared identifiers. A knowledge graph with an explicit ontology is the natural fix: Claude reads the documents and extracts entities, the ontology says what may connect to what, and the graph answers multi-hop questions ("which budget head paid for this road, who built it, and is it still under warranty?") that no single source can.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: File Contents 00-shared-foundation.md Ontology, graph database choice (HydraDB and alternatives), data sources, architecture, how Claude is used, risks. All five ideas build on this. 01-paisa-trail.md Follow one rupee from budget head to the street. 02-vachan-tracker.md Promise tracker: every civic promise linked to evidence of delivery. 03-thekedar-graph.md Contractor and procurement red-flag graph. 04-jawabdar.md "Who is responsible for this?" Photo to responsible agency, officer post, contractor and a drafted complaint or RTI. 05-ward-lens.md Ward scorecards: spend against outcomes, with citizen-verified ground truth. 06-prep-and-day-plan.md What to do between now and the 21st, and an hour-by-hour plan for the day. 08-multi-agent-system.md The agent team behind the ideas, on Claude Managed Agents: intake, audit and citizen desks, safeguards, and how to run it. managed-agents/ Agent definitions, rubrics, the Python client that runs sessions, and a LangGraph pipeline that orders the steps and pauses for human review. Not yet applied or run against the API. 07-tender-portals.md What the BMC tender portal and Mahatenders publish, their identifiers, how they map to the graph, and how to collect from them.

docs.title: The five ideas, ranked
docs.text:
# Idea Challenge pillar Demo strength Data risk Adoption path 1 Paisa Trail See where money is spent High Medium: needs budget and tender PDFs parsed BMC finance and IT; newsrooms 2 Jawabdar Hold the right people accountable Very high: photo in, answer out Medium: needs road-to-agency mapping Ward offices; 1916 helpline 3 Vachan Tracker Track promises High Low: budget speech and news are public text Corporators; civil society 4 Thekedar Graph Accountability High, but legally sensitive High: entity resolution, company data Vigilance department; journalists 5 Ward Lens See spending and outcomes Medium High: outcome data is patchy Ward committees; citizen groups

More ideas: a further 35, rated for value and feasibility, are listed in ../mumbai-civic-ideas/.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
Build Paisa Trail as the spine, with Jawabdar as the front door.

  • Paisa Trail produces the graph every other idea needs (budget head → work → contract → contractor → asset → ward).
  • Jawabdar is the most persuasive two-minute demo: a citizen photographs a broken road and gets back who built it, what it cost, whether the contractor still owes repairs, and a ready-to-file complaint.
  • Scope it to one ward and one department (roads). A complete, sourced graph of one ward beats a thin graph of the whole city, and judges from civic bodies will test it on roads they know.
  • Vachan Tracker is the natural third layer if the team has spare hands, since it reuses the same work nodes.

How it is built: as a team of agents, not a single chatbot. An intake desk reads and verifies documents, an audit desk writes findings that a Challenger agent attacks before a person sees them, and a citizen desk answers residents. See 08-multi-agent-system.md. Two mechanisms there are worth leading the pitch with: every gap in the graph becomes a drafted RTI application, and defects on roads still under contractor liability become a weekly list for the ward officer.

Thekedar Graph and Ward Lens are worth pitching as the roadmap, not building on the day: the first needs legal review before anything is published, the second needs outcome data that takes weeks to assemble.

docs.title: What is verified and what is not
docs.text:
Facts in these plans were checked on 15 November 2026 where possible. Items to confirm before relying on them:

  • HydraDB details come from its GitHub README. It is a young project (v0.3) and the Cypher subset it accepts must be checked against its cypher-compat.md before committing. Every plan here keeps Neo4j as a drop-in fallback over the same Bolt driver.
  • Tender portals were examined directly; see 07-tender-portals.md. Listing pages on Mahatenders sit behind a captcha, so tender detail and award pages were not opened.
  • Other data source availability was not tested end to end. 06-prep-and-day-plan.md starts with a data spike for exactly this reason.
  • The agent system in managed-agents/ was syntax-checked against the Python SDK but not run; no API credential was available when it was written.
  • Budget figures are from press coverage of the 2026-27 BMC budget, not from the budget books themselves.

docs.title: Shared foundation
docs.text: Everything the five ideas have in common: the ontology, the graph database, the data, the pipeline and the rules for using Claude. Build this once.

docs.title: 1. The problem in numbers
docs.text:
• BMC's 2026-27 budget is ₹80,952.56 crore, of which about ₹48,164 crore is capital works (press reports of the budget presentation).
  • Civic data reported in the press showed more than half of the 2025-26 capital allocation unspent late in that year.
  • On road concretisation, press reports from 2025 put Phase 1 at 46 km complete out of 324 km, with contractors fined and blacklisted for delays and poor quality.

A citizen can read each of those facts in a newspaper. What they cannot do is start from their road and find the budget line, the contractor and the deadline. That is the gap.

docs.title: 2. Mumbai Civic Ontology (MCO)
docs.text: A small ontology, written once in OWL/Turtle, that every idea shares. Reuse established vocabularies rather than inventing terms, so the result is recognisable to civic-tech people and exportable.

docs.title: Vocabularies to reuse
docs.text: Need Vocabulary Tenders, awards, contracts, payments Open Contracting Data Standard (OCDS) concepts Departments, posts, reporting lines W3C Organization Ontology (org:) People, posts, memberships of elected bodies Popolo Where every fact came from W3C PROV-O (prov:) Ward boundaries, road geometry GeoSPARQL Budget head hierarchy, work categories SKOS Validity periods, deadlines OWL-Time
