docs.title: Three rules that make the graph trustworthy
docs.text:
1. Every fact has a source. Each node and relationship carries source_id, page, quote, extracted_at, confidence. No source, no edge. The UI shows the quote and links to the page.
  2. Every fact has a trust tier. official (BMC document), reported (news), citizen (unverified upload), derived (computed by us). Answers say which tier they rest on.
  3. Facts are dated, not overwritten. valid_from / valid_to on relationships. A revised deadline is a new edge, so slippage is visible as history.

docs.title: Keep the ontology in Turtle, compile it to the property graph
docs.text:
• ontology/mco.ttl is the source of truth: classes, properties, domains and ranges.
  • ontology/shapes.ttl holds SHACL shapes (a Contract must have exactly one Award; an amount must be a positive decimal with a currency).
  • A small script generates three things from those files: the JSON schema Claude must fill during extraction, the validation step in the pipeline (pySHACL over an rdflib graph of each batch), and the label and relationship whitelist for the property graph.

This gives ontology discipline without needing a reasoner inside the database.

docs.title: HydraDB, as asked
docs.text:
From its README: HydraDB is a distributed graph database in Rust, built on SlateDB with S3-compatible object storage as the source of truth, with traversal on SuiteSparse GraphBLAS. It speaks a practical OpenCypher subset over Neo4j-compatible Bolt 5.x and an HTTP JSON API. Licence is Elastic License 2.0.

For this project Against Bolt-compatible, so the standard neo4j Python and JS drivers work v0.3; young, few independent evaluations Object storage backend makes it cheap to host a public, read-heavy civic dataset Cypher is a subset: check MERGE, DETACH DELETE and multi-row mutations against cypher-compat.md Built-in path procedures (algo.SPpaths, algo.SSpaths) suit "follow the money" queries README mentions no vector or full-text index, so those live elsewhere Per-graph namespaces map well to "one graph per city or agency" Needs building from source or a container image; allow setup time

ELv2 permits self-hosting and modification. It forbids offering the database itself as a managed service, which does not affect a civic app built on top of it.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Database Model Why consider it Caveat Neo4j Community Property graph, Cypher Default choice; vector and full-text indexes built in; neosemantics imports RDF/OWL directly; Graph Data Science for community detection JVM memory footprint; GPLv3 FalkorDB Property graph, Cypher, GraphBLAS Fast; vector index; aimed at GraphRAG Source-available licence; check terms Memgraph Property graph, Cypher In-memory, Neo4j-driver compatible BSL licence Kuzu Embedded property graph Zero-ops, runs in-process; ideal for a laptop demo Community-maintained now Apache Jena Fuseki / Oxigraph / Ontotext GraphDB RDF triple store, SPARQL Native OWL and SHACL, real inference Slower to build an app on; weaker path queries

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Primary store: HydraDB, accessed only through the Bolt driver and a thin repository layer.
  • Fallback: Neo4j Community in Docker, same driver, same queries. Decide by the end of the pre-event spike. If HydraDB rejects a query shape the app needs, switch and lose nothing.
  • Ontology and validation: Turtle + SHACL in the pipeline (rdflib, pySHACL), not in the database.
  • Text search and embeddings: Postgres with pgvector (or SQLite with FTS5 for the demo), keyed by graph node id. Used to find the starting node; the graph does the reasoning.

Write all Cypher inside the subset HydraDB documents: typed relationships, bounded variable-length paths, OPTIONAL MATCH, aggregation, UNWIND batch writes. Avoid APOC and Neo4j-only procedures so the fallback works in both directions.

docs.text:
Confirm each of these in the pre-event spike. Format and availability change without notice.

The two tender portals are covered in detail in 07-tender-portals.md, including identifiers, field mapping and how to collect without defeating the captcha.

MumbaiSpend (IndiaSpend, 2017) once published BMC vendor and purchase-order data. Check whether it is still live; if so it is the best single seed for Contractor and Payment nodes.

Ask the organisers now whether the problem briefing comes with data from BMC. If it does, most of the "High" rows become easy.

docs.title: 5. Architecture
docs.text:
┌───────────── Sources (PDF, web, CSV, photos) ─────────────┐
            ▼                                                            │
   1. Fetch and archive      raw file + hash + URL + fetched_at          │
            ▼                                                            │
   2. Parse                  PDF text / OCR / tables; Marathi kept as-is │
            ▼                                                            │
   3. Extract (Claude)       JSON constrained by the ontology schema,    │
                             with page and verbatim quote per fact       │
            ▼                                                            │
   4. Validate               SHACL shapes; reject or queue for review    │
            ▼                                                            │
   5. Resolve entities       same contractor, road, ward across sources  │
            ▼                                                            │
   6. Load                   UNWIND batches over Bolt → HydraDB          │
            ▼                                                            │
   7. Serve                  API + MCP server ── Claude agent ── Web/WhatsApp UI

Suggested stack: Python (FastAPI, neo4j driver, rdflib, pySHACL, PyMuPDF), Postgres with pgvector, a Next.js or plain React front end with MapLibre for maps.

docs.title: Serving through MCP
docs.text:
Expose the graph as a small MCP server rather than letting the model write free-form Cypher against a public dataset:

Tool Purpose find_entity(text, type?) Fuzzy and semantic lookup to a node id locate(lat, lon) Asset, ward and owning agency at a point trace_money(node_id) Budget head ↔ work ↔ contract ↔ payments path who_is_responsible(node_id) Agency, department, post, current holder, contractor under liability work_status(work_id) Milestones, deadlines, revisions, penalties cypher_read(query) Read-only escape hatch, with a label whitelist and row limit get_source(source_id, page) The quote and link behind any fact

Every tool returns facts with their source_id and trust tier, so the agent can cite. The same server works from Claude Desktop, Claude Code or the web app, which is a useful point when pitching adoption: BMC staff and journalists can query it with tools they already have.

docs.title: 6. How Claude is used
docs.text:
Job Notes Document extraction One document at a time, schema-constrained output, quote and page mandatory. Use a larger model for committee resolutions and a small fast one for routine tender notices. Marathi and Hindi Extract directly from Marathi text; store the original name and an English transliteration on each node. Entity resolution Blocking by normalised name and ward, then Claude adjudicates candidate pairs with a reason. Never auto-merge people. Question answering Agent over the MCP tools. System prompt requires a citation for every figure and an explicit "the data does not show this" when the graph is silent. Drafting Complaints, RTI applications, plain-language summaries, in the citizen's language. Vision Classify a citizen photo (pothole, open drain, incomplete work) and read any contractor signboard in frame.

Rules that keep it honest:

  • The model never states an amount, date or name that is not in a tool result.
  • Derived judgements ("delayed", "over budget") are computed by code from dated facts, then explained by the model.
  • A human-review queue holds low-confidence extractions and all entity merges involving people.
  • Keep an evaluation set: 30 questions with hand-checked answers for the demo ward. Run it after every pipeline change.

docs.title: 7. Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Defamation: the graph links named contractors and officials to failures Show sourced facts, not conclusions. Label red flags as "patterns worth checking". Refer to officials by post. Offer a right of reply. Get a lawyer on the team to review wording; the event invites them. Wrong extraction published as fact Quote and page on every fact; trust tiers; review queue; a "report an error" link on every card Personal data (DPDP Act 2023) Elected representatives and officials in their public role only. No home addresses or phone numbers. Blur faces and number plates in citizen photos. Data is not available on the day Pre-load one ward before the event; never demo from live scraping HydraDB immaturity Bolt-only access and Neo4j fallback, decided before the event Scraping terms and load Fetch politely, cache everything, prefer published files and OpenCity datasets Adoption stalls after the event Publish the ontology and the cleaned dataset openly; give BMC a version that runs on their own data and needs no new data entry

docs.title: 8. What adoption looks like
docs.text:
The pitch to civic authorities is not "we will expose you". It is: you already publish all of this; we make it legible, and it reduces your RTI and complaint load. Concretely offer:

  1. A one-ward pilot with the ward office, using only documents BMC already publishes.
  2. The ontology as a proposed publishing format, so future tenders and work orders arrive as data.
  3. A weekly digest for the ward officer: works at risk of missing deadlines, defects reported on roads still under contractor liability.

docs.title: Idea 1: Paisa Trail
docs.text:
Follow one rupee from the budget book to the street.

Read 00-shared-foundation.md first. This plan covers only what is specific to this idea.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text: The BMC budget is published by budget head. Works are tendered by tender number. Contracts are sanctioned by committee resolution number. Roads are known to citizens by name. None of these identifiers appear in each other's documents consistently, so nobody outside the system can connect "₹X crore for roads in the budget" to "this road outside my house".

docs.title: What the citizen gets
docs.text:
• Search or tap a map: pick a road, a ward or a budget head.
  • The trail: budget head → allocation this year → work → tender → contractor → contract value → payments (where known) → current status. Each hop shows its source page.
  • Ask in plain language, in English, Hindi or Marathi: "How much was allocated for storm water drains in K/West this year and what has started?"
  • The gaps are shown, not hidden. Where a hop is missing ("tender found, no award found"), the trail says so. Those gaps are themselves the accountability finding.

docs.title: User stories
docs.text:
1. As a resident, I enter my road name and see what was sanctioned for it, who is doing the work and when it is due.
  2. As a journalist, I pick a budget head and see every work funded under it, sorted by amount, with the unspent remainder.
  3. As a corporator, I see all works in my electoral ward with status, to raise in committee.
  4. As a BMC finance officer, I see allocations with no linked tender six months into the year.

docs.title: Graph slice
docs.text:
(FiscalYear)<-[:FOR_YEAR]-(Allocation)-[:UNDER]->(BudgetHead)-[:PARENT_OF*0..4]->(BudgetHead)
(Work)-[:FUNDED_BY]->(Allocation)
(Work)-[:IMPROVES]->(Asset)-[:LOCATED_IN]->(AdminWard)
(Tender)-[:FOR_WORK]->(Work)
(Award)-[:OF]->(Tender)
(Contract)-[:FROM_AWARD]->(Award)
(Contractor)-[:PARTY_TO]->(Contract)
(Payment)-[:UNDER_CONTRACT]->(Contract)

Tender.id is the Mahatenders id (for example 2026_MCGM_1303610_1); Tender.bmc_bid_no is the ten-digit number on the BMC notice. Award value and contractor come from Mahatenders' Results of Tenders. See 07-tender-portals.md.

Key properties: Allocation.amount_be, amount_re, amount_actual; Tender.estimated_cost, tender_no, published_on; Contract.value, signed_on, due_on; Work.status, category.

docs.title: Example queries
docs.text:
Trail for a road:

MATCH (a:Asset {id: $asset_id})<-[:IMPROVES]-(w:Work)
OPTIONAL MATCH (w)-[:FUNDED_BY]->(al:Allocation)-[:UNDER]->(bh:BudgetHead)
OPTIONAL MATCH (t:Tender)-[:FOR_WORK]->(w)
OPTIONAL MATCH (aw:Award)-[:OF]->(t)
OPTIONAL MATCH (c:Contract)-[:FROM_AWARD]->(aw)
OPTIONAL MATCH (k:Contractor)-[:PARTY_TO]->(c)
RETURN w, al, bh, t, c, k
ORDER BY t.published_on DESC

Allocations with nothing tendered against them:

MATCH (al:Allocation)-[:FOR_YEAR]->(:FiscalYear {label: '2026-27'})
MATCH (al)-[:UNDER]->(bh:BudgetHead)
OPTIONAL MATCH (w:Work)-[:FUNDED_BY]->(al)
WITH bh, al, count(w) AS works
WHERE works = 0
RETURN bh.code, bh.name, al.amount_be
ORDER BY al.amount_be DESC
LIMIT 50

docs.title: The hard part: linking a work to its budget head
docs.text:
Tender notices rarely print the budget code cleanly. Use a three-step linker and record which step made each link:

  1. Explicit: the budget code appears in the tender or resolution text. Trust tier official.
  2. Structural: department + work category + ward narrows to one budget head. Tier derived, with the rule recorded.
  3. Semantic: Claude ranks candidate budget heads from the description and explains the choice. Tier derived, confidence stored, shown to the user as "probable".

Never present a step 2 or 3 link as certain.

docs.title: Before the event (see 06-prep-and-day-plan.md)
docs.text: Step Output Pick the demo ward and department (roads) A named scope Collect the roads budget pages for 2026-27 and 2025-26 2 PDFs, archived with hashes Collect 40 to 60 tenders for that ward from Mahatenders (detail and AOC pages) with the matching BMC notice PDFs, plus any committee resolutions Raw corpus Draft mco.ttl and the extraction schema for BudgetHead, Allocation, Tender, Work, Contract, Contractor Schema v0 Stand up HydraDB and Neo4j; run the same five queries on both Database decision Hand-label 10 documents Gold set for measuring extraction

docs.title: Build phases
docs.text: Phase Work Done when 1. Budget tree Parse budget tables into BudgetHead hierarchy and Allocations; reconcile sub-totals to the printed totals Sum of leaves equals printed department total 2. Tender extraction Claude extracts Tender and Work with quote and page; SHACL validation 90% field accuracy on the gold set 3. Asset matching Match road names in tenders to OpenStreetMap ways within the ward; store geometry 80% of works placed on the map 4. Award and contract Take AOC records from Mahatenders; fill gaps from committee resolutions and the concretisation dashboard; resolve contractor names Contractor attached to at least half of the works 5. Budget linker Three-step linker above Every work has a link or an explicit "unlinked" flag 6. MCP tools find_entity, locate, trace_money, get_source Agent answers the 30 evaluation questions with citations 7. UI Map, trail view as a horizontal chain of cards, chat panel, source drawer Demo script runs offline

docs.title: Team split (4 to 5 people)
docs.text: Role Owns Data lead Corpus, parsing, gold set Graph lead Ontology, loader, queries, database AI lead Extraction prompts, linker, agent, evaluation Front end Map, trail view, chat Domain and pitch Checks facts against reality, adoption story, demo script

docs.title: Demo script (3 minutes)
docs.text:
1. "Here is a road in our ward everyone knows is dug up." Tap it on the map.
  2. The trail appears: budget head, allocation, tender, contractor, due date. Open one source card to show the original page and highlighted quote.
  3. Ask in Marathi: "या वॉर्डमध्ये रस्त्यांसाठी किती पैसे मंजूर झाले आणि किती कामे सुरू झाली?" The agent answers with figures and citations.
  4. Show the "allocated but never tendered" list for the ward.
  5. Close: "This used only documents BMC already publishes. Give us one ward office and we can keep it current."

docs.title: Success measures
docs.text:
• Coverage: share of the ward's road allocation that is traced to at least a tender.
  • Accuracy: extraction accuracy on the gold set; zero uncited figures in agent answers.
  • Usefulness: a person who lives in the ward finds their road and learns something they did not know.

docs.title: Risks specific to this idea
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Budget books are scanned images OCR, then Claude vision on table pages; verify totals arithmetically Payments data is not public Show the trail up to contract value; mark payments "not published" and name the RTI that would obtain it City-wide works do not map to one ward Model them as Work with scope: citywide; exclude from ward totals and say so

docs.title: Idea 2: Vachan Tracker
docs.text:
Every civic promise, linked to evidence of whether it was kept.

Read 00-shared-foundation.md first.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text: Promises are made in budget speeches, manifestos, press conferences and committee meetings. Delivery, if it happens, is recorded in tender portals and work dashboards. Nobody connects the two, so a promise quietly expires and reappears in next year's speech.

docs.title: What the citizen gets
docs.text:
• A list of promises for their ward or for the city, each with a status: Kept, In progress, Delayed, Stalled, No evidence, Dropped.
  • The status is not an opinion. It is computed from linked evidence, and each promise shows that evidence: the tender, the work order, the completion note, the news report, the citizen photo.
  • A history view: the same promise across years, with deadline changes shown ("promised for May 2025, then May 2026, then December 2026").
  • Follow a promise and get notified when its evidence changes.

docs.title: What counts as a promise
docs.text:
A statement is a Promise only if it has: a maker (person or agency), a deliverable (what will exist), and ideally a quantity, place and deadline. "We are committed to better roads" is not a promise. "All roads in the island city will be concretised by May 2027" is.

Claude classifies each candidate sentence and extracts those fields. Vague statements are stored as Statement and not tracked.

docs.title: Graph slice
docs.text:
(Promise)-[:MADE_BY]->(Person|Agency)
(Promise)-[:MADE_IN]->(SourceDocument)        // speech, manifesto, press report
(Promise)-[:ABOUT]->(Asset|AdminWard|BudgetHead)
(Promise)-[:RESTATES]->(Promise)              // same promise in a later year
(Promise)-[:FULFILLED_BY]->(Work)
(Promise)-[:FUNDED_BY]->(Allocation)
(Evidence)-[:BEARS_ON {direction: 'supports'|'contradicts'}]->(Promise)

Promise properties: text_original, text_en, deliverable, quantity, unit, deadline, made_on, specificity_score.

docs.title: Status rules
docs.text:
Computed in code, re-run nightly. The model explains the result; it does not decide it.

Status Rule Kept Linked work has a completion record at or above the promised quantity In progress Linked work has a contract and no missed milestone Delayed Deadline passed, or a later promise RESTATES it with a later deadline Stalled Contract exists; no evidence of activity in the last 180 days No evidence No allocation, tender or work could be linked Dropped Official statement cancelling it, or allocation removed in the next budget

docs.title: Example queries
docs.text:
Promises restated with a slipping deadline:

MATCH (p2:Promise)-[:RESTATES]->(p1:Promise)
WHERE p2.deadline > p1.deadline
RETURN p1.text_en, p1.deadline AS first_deadline, p2.deadline AS new_deadline, p2.made_on
ORDER BY p2.made_on DESC

Promises about a ward with no money behind them:

MATCH (p:Promise)-[:ABOUT]->(:AdminWard {code: $ward})
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:FUNDED_BY]->(al:Allocation)
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:FULFILLED_BY]->(w:Work)
WITH p, count(al) AS funded, count(w) AS works
WHERE funded = 0 AND works = 0
RETURN p.text_en, p.made_on, p.deadline

docs.title: Sources, in order of ease
docs.text:
1. Commissioner's budget speeches for 2025-26 and 2026-27 (two speeches make RESTATES detection possible).
  2. Party manifestos from the most recent BMC election.
  3. News reports of announcements, English and Marathi.
  4. Standing Committee resolutions.

docs.title: Build phases
docs.text: Phase Work Done when 1. Promise extraction Split speeches into statements; Claude classifies and extracts fields with quote and page 100+ promises from two budget speeches, spot-checked 2. Deduplicate and chain Embed promises; Claude adjudicates near-duplicates across years into RESTATES chains Chains reviewed by a human for the demo ward 3. Link to delivery Match promise to Works and Allocations (shares the Paisa Trail graph); candidates by ward, category and embedding, then Claude picks with a reason Each promise has links or an explicit "no evidence" 4. Status engine Rules above as a Python module with unit tests Status reproducible from the graph alone 5. Evidence intake News monitoring for the tracked promises; citizen photo upload with location New evidence changes a status in the demo 6. UI Promise cards, timeline per promise, ward filter, share-as-image card for WhatsApp Demo script runs

docs.title: If building standalone, without Paisa Trail
docs.text: Skip phase 3's tender linkage and rely on news and citizen evidence. The tracker is still useful, but statuses will mostly be "reported" tier rather than "official".

docs.title: Demo script
docs.text:
1. Open the 2026-27 budget speech. Show 60 promises extracted, each with its sentence highlighted in the original.
  2. Filter to the demo ward. Show one Kept, one Delayed with its deadline history across two speeches, one No evidence.
  3. Upload a photo of an unfinished site; the linked promise gains a citizen-tier evidence item.
  4. Generate the shareable card: promise, status, three sources.

docs.title: Success measures
docs.text:
• Precision of promise extraction: of items shown as promises, how many a human agrees are concrete commitments (target above 90%).
  • Share of promises with at least one official-tier evidence link.
  • Number of multi-year chains found; these are the most newsworthy output.

docs.title: Risks specific to this idea
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Seen as partisan Track every maker by the same rules; publish the rules; show kept promises as prominently as broken ones Wrong link makes a kept promise look broken "No evidence" is worded as "we found no evidence", with a button for the maker's office to submit some Vague promises resist tracking Publish a specificity score; that itself nudges better promises

docs.title: Idea 3: Thekedar Graph
docs.text:
A contractor and procurement graph that surfaces patterns worth checking.

Read 00-shared-foundation.md first.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
Press reports describe contractors fined or blacklisted for poor road work, and penalties that go unrecovered for months. What the public cannot see is the pattern across contracts: who keeps winning, whether a blacklisted firm's directors reappear under another name, whether the same few bidders rotate, whether penalised firms still receive new awards.

These are graph questions. They are also the questions where a wrong answer does the most damage, so this idea needs the most care.

docs.title: What the user gets
docs.text:
Primary users are journalists, auditors, vigilance staff and civil society researchers, not the general public.

  • Contractor profile: all contracts, total value, wards, on-time record, penalties, blacklisting periods, related entities.
  • Red flags, each a named, documented pattern with the underlying records attached.
  • Network view: contractors, companies, directors and addresses, with shared links highlighted.
  • Ask: "Which contractors penalised in 2025 received new awards within twelve months?"

docs.title: Red flag catalogue
docs.text:
Based on widely used open-contracting red flag indicators. Each is a deterministic query; the model only explains results.

Flag Pattern Award after penalty New Award dated inside or shortly after a Penalty or Blacklisting period Reappearing directors A director of a blacklisted company is a director of another company that then wins Shared identity Two bidders on the same tender share an address, phone, email or director Single bidder Tender with one valid bid Concentration One contractor holds more than a set share of a ward's or department's contract value Bid rotation A small set of bidders repeatedly co-bid and take turns winning Cost escalation Contract value revised upward beyond a threshold after award Just under threshold Clusters of contract values just below an approval limit Short tender window Days between publication and closing below the norm Chronic delay Share of a contractor's works past due date

docs.title: Graph slice
docs.text:
(Contractor)-[:IS]->(Company)
(Director)-[:DIRECTOR_OF {from,to}]->(Company)
(Company)-[:REGISTERED_AT]->(Address)
(Contractor)-[:SUBMITTED]->(Bid)-[:ON]->(Tender)
(Award)-[:OF]->(Tender)    (Award)-[:TO]->(Contractor)
(Penalty)-[:IMPOSED_ON]->(Contractor)    (Penalty)-[:FOR_WORK]->(Work)
(Blacklisting {from,to})-[:OF]->(Contractor)
(Contractor)-[:JOINT_VENTURE_WITH]->(Contractor)

docs.title: Example queries
docs.text:
Awards after a penalty:

MATCH (p:Penalty)-[:IMPOSED_ON]->(k:Contractor)<-[:TO]-(a:Award)
WHERE a.date > p.date AND a.date < p.date + duration({months: 12})
RETURN k.name, p.date, p.amount, a.date, a.value
ORDER BY a.value DESC

If the chosen database does not support duration arithmetic, precompute p.window_end at load time and compare dates directly.

Co-bidders sharing a director:

MATCH (k1:Contractor)-[:SUBMITTED]->(:Bid)-[:ON]->(t:Tender)<-[:ON]-(:Bid)<-[:SUBMITTED]-(k2:Contractor)
WHERE k1.id < k2.id
MATCH (k1)-[:IS]->(:Company)<-[:DIRECTOR_OF]-(d:Director)-[:DIRECTOR_OF]->(:Company)<-[:IS]-(k2)
RETURN t.tender_no, k1.name, k2.name, d.name

Paths between a blacklisted firm and a recent winner, using a bounded traversal:

MATCH (b:Contractor {id: $blacklisted}), (w:Contractor {id: $winner})
MATCH path = (b)-[:IS|DIRECTOR_OF|REGISTERED_AT*1..4]-(w)
RETURN path LIMIT 10

Rotation and concentration need community detection. HydraDB's README lists path and degree procedures only, so compute communities offline in Python (NetworkX, Louvain) and write community_id back onto nodes.

docs.title: Entity resolution, the core difficulty
docs.text:
The same firm appears as "M/s ABC Infra Pvt Ltd", "ABC Infrastructure" and "A.B.C. Infra (JV)".

  1. Normalise: strip "M/s", legal suffixes, punctuation; transliterate Marathi.
  2. Block: candidates sharing a normalised token set, a registration number, or an address.
  3. Adjudicate: Claude compares each candidate pair with all known attributes and returns same, different or unsure, with a reason.
  4. Merge only on "same" with a hard identifier (registration number, tax id) or after human approval. "Unsure" pairs get a POSSIBLY_SAME_AS edge that is displayed as such and never used to raise a flag on its own.
  5. Never merge natural persons on name alone. Two directors called "R. Shah" stay separate until a director identification number matches.

docs.title: Implementation plan
docs.text:
Phase Work Done when 1. Award corpus Awards, Contractors and values from Mahatenders AOC records, then committee resolutions and the concretisation dashboard 200+ awards loaded 2. Penalty corpus Extract Penalty and Blacklisting events from BMC press notes and news, with dates and amounts Each event has an official or reported source 3. Entity resolution Pipeline above with a review screen Reviewed contractor list for the demo scope 4. Company layer Add Company, Director, Address for the top 30 contractors by value, from public company records Manual for the hackathon; automate later 5. Flag engine One query per flag, results stored as RedFlag nodes linked to their evidence Flags reproducible; each has an evidence bundle 6. UI Profile page, flag list with filters, network view Demo script runs 7. Legal pass Lawyer reviews every label and sentence on screen Sign-off before anything public

Mahatenders is the source for awards (Results of Tenders) and blacklisting (Debarment List); see 07-tender-portals.md. Bid-level data (who bid and lost) depends on whether its Tenders Status pages list all bidders, which must be confirmed. If it is unavailable, drop the flags that need it (shared identity among co-bidders, single bidder, rotation) and say so. The award-after-penalty and reappearing-director flags need only award and penalty data.

docs.title: Publication rules
docs.text:
These are requirements, not suggestions.

  • The interface says "pattern worth checking", never "fraud", "corrupt" or "cartel".
  • Every flag opens to the records behind it. No flag without at least one official-tier source.
  • Before public release, a named contractor is given the chance to respond, and the response is shown beside the flag.
  • Access to the network view is limited to registered researchers and journalists at first; the public sees contractor profiles and penalties from official sources.
  • Officials appear by post, not by name, unless named in an official order.

docs.title: Demo script
docs.text:
1. Open a contractor profile: contracts, wards, penalties, all sourced.
  2. Show the "award after penalty" list. Open one and walk through the two source documents.
  3. Network view: two firms linked through a shared director, one of them barred from tendering.
  4. State plainly what the tool does not claim, and show the right-of-reply field.

For the hackathon demo, consider anonymising contractor names on screen (Contractor A, B, C) unless every displayed fact has been checked by the team's lawyer.

docs.title: Success measures
docs.text:
• Entity resolution precision on a hand-checked sample (target above 95%; a false merge is the worst failure).
  • Share of flags a domain expert judges worth a follow-up question.
  • One finding a journalist or official on the judging panel did not already know.

docs.title: Why this is roadmap, not day-one
docs.text: High data difficulty, high legal exposure, and its users are specialists. It becomes much stronger once Paisa Trail has built the award data it depends on. Pitch it as phase two.

docs.title: Idea 4: Jawabdar
docs.text:
"Who is responsible for this?" A photo in, the accountable agency, post and contractor out, with a complaint ready to file.

Read 00-shared-foundation.md first.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
In Mumbai, the road outside your building may belong to BMC, MMRDA, MSRDC, the state PWD, MHADA, the railways or the port authority. Inside BMC it may fall to the ward office or to a central department. The trench in it may have been dug by a utility. Citizens complain to the wrong body, the complaint is closed as "not ours", and nothing happens.

There is a second, less known lever: works are usually covered by a defect liability period, during which the contractor must repair defects at their own cost. If a newly built road cracks inside that period, the right demand is not "please fix it" but "make the contractor fix it, as the contract requires". Citizens almost never know a road is under liability.

docs.title: What the citizen gets
docs.text:
1. Take a photo or drop a pin. On WhatsApp or the web.
  2. Get back, in their language:
  3. Whose it is: the owning agency and department.
  4. Who is accountable: the post responsible (for example the ward's Assistant Engineer, Roads), and the escalation chain above it.
  5. The work history: last work on this asset, contractor, cost, completion date.
  6. Liability status: "This road was completed in March 2025 and is under contractor liability until March 2030" (dates from the contract, where known).
  7. The elected representative for that electoral ward.
  8. A drafted complaint addressed to the right office, citing the work order and the liability clause, plus an optional RTI application asking for the inspection reports.
  9. A tracking link. If the complaint is not resolved in the service-level time, a drafted escalation to the next post up.

docs.title: Why a graph
docs.text:
The answer is a traversal across four different hierarchies that meet at a point on the map:

(point) → Asset → OWNED_BY → Agency → Department → Post → HOLDS ← Person
                → LOCATED_IN → AdminWard → ElectoralWard ← REPRESENTS ← Person
                ← IMPROVES ← Work ← Contract ← PARTY_TO ← Contractor
                                  → DefectLiabilityPeriod {from, to}
          Post → REPORTS_TO* → Post         (escalation chain)

docs.title: Graph slice
docs.text:
(Agency)-[:OWNS]->(Asset)
(Department)-[:PART_OF]->(Agency)
(Department)-[:MAINTAINS {category}]->(AssetType)
(Post)-[:IN]->(Department)
(Post)-[:COVERS]->(AdminWard)
(Post)-[:REPORTS_TO]->(Post)
(Person)-[:HOLDS {from,to}]->(Post)
(Work)-[:HAS_DLP]->(DefectLiabilityPeriod)
(IssueType)-[:HANDLED_BY]->(Department)           // pothole → Roads; open manhole → Sewerage
(IssueType)-[:HAS_SLA {days}]->(ServiceStandard)
(Complaint)-[:ABOUT]->(Asset)   (Complaint)-[:ROUTED_TO]->(Post)   (Complaint)-[:ESCALATED_TO]->(Post)

The IssueType → Department routing table is small (about 40 issue types) and can be written by hand from BMC's published complaint categories.

docs.title: Example queries
docs.text:
Who is responsible, given an asset and an issue type:

MATCH (a:Asset {id: $asset_id})-[:LOCATED_IN]->(w:AdminWard)
MATCH (ag:Agency)-[:OWNS]->(a)
MATCH (it:IssueType {code: $issue})-[:HANDLED_BY]->(d:Department)-[:PART_OF]->(ag)
MATCH (p:Post)-[:IN]->(d)
MATCH (p)-[:COVERS]->(w)
OPTIONAL MATCH (per:Person)-[h:HOLDS]->(p) WHERE h.to IS NULL
RETURN ag.name, d.name, p.title, per.name

Escalation chain:

MATCH (p:Post {id: $post_id})-[:REPORTS_TO*1..4]->(up:Post)
RETURN up.title, up.office

Is the asset under contractor liability today:

MATCH (a:Asset {id: $asset_id})<-[:IMPROVES]-(w:Work)-[:HAS_DLP]->(d:DefectLiabilityPeriod)
WHERE d.from <= $today AND d.to >= $today
MATCH (k:Contractor)-[:PARTY_TO]->(:Contract)-[:FOR_WORK]->(w)
RETURN w.title, k.name, d.to

docs.title: Data to assemble
docs.text: Data Source Effort Road geometry and names for the demo ward OpenStreetMap Low Ward boundaries, administrative and electoral OpenCity or BMC files Low Road ownership (which roads are not BMC's) Agency project maps, news, local knowledge; start with a short list of known non-BMC roads in the ward Medium, manual BMC ward office structure: posts and reporting lines BMC website, proactive disclosures under RTI Act section 4 Medium Issue type to department routing BMC complaint categories Low, manual Recent works and contractors on each road Paisa Trail graph, or the concretisation dashboard directly Medium Works by other agencies in the ward Mahatenders lists MMRDA, MSRDC, PWD, MHADA and BEST tenders alongside BMC's Medium Defect liability terms General conditions in the BMC tender notice PDF for each work Medium; Claude extracts the clause and period Corporators by electoral ward Public lists Low

docs.title: Build phases
docs.text: Phase Work Done when 1. Locate Point → nearest road segment → ward → electoral ward, using PostGIS or Shapely Correct for 20 test points 2. Org graph Agencies, departments, posts, reporting lines, routing table for the demo ward "Who is responsible" query returns a post for every issue type 3. Work and liability Link works to road segments; extract liability period from tender conditions; compute from and to 15+ roads in the ward with liability dates 4. Photo understanding Claude vision: issue type, severity, any signboard text; ask one clarifying question if unsure 9 of 10 test photos classified correctly 5. Drafting Complaint and RTI templates filled from graph facts; English, Hindi, Marathi A lawyer on the team approves the templates 6. Channel Web app first; WhatsApp through a business API sandbox if time allows Photo to answer in under 20 seconds 7. Tracking Store complaint, due date from the service standard, drafted escalation Escalation draft appears when the clock is advanced

docs.title: Agent design
docs.text:
One agent with the MCP tools locate, who_is_responsible, work_status, trace_money, get_source. Instructions:

  • Ask for location if the photo has none. Never guess a location from the image.
  • State ownership with its trust tier. If ownership is uncertain, say "probably BMC; if they say it is not theirs, here is who else it could be".
  • Name posts, not people, in the drafted complaint, unless the person is an elected representative.
  • Cite the work order and liability clause only when they are in the graph.

docs.title: Filing
docs.text: Do not automate submission into government portals at the hackathon. Give the citizen the draft, the right channel (BMC's helpline, app or ward office; the state RTI portal) and a one-tap copy. Automated filing is something to negotiate with BMC as part of adoption.

docs.title: Demo script (2 minutes)
docs.text:
1. On a phone, photograph a cracked concrete road (a prepared image with location).
  2. The reply appears: BMC, Roads department of the ward, the responsible post, the contractor, completed on a given date, under contractor liability until a given date, with a link to the contract clause.
  3. Tap "Draft complaint". It appears in Marathi, citing the work and the clause.
  4. Second pin, on a road owned by another agency: the answer changes to that agency and its grievance channel. This is the moment the audience understands the routing problem.
  5. Show the ward officer's view: open defects on roads still under liability, grouped by contractor. "This is money the city does not need to spend."

docs.title: Why authorities might adopt it
docs.text:
• Fewer misrouted complaints reaching the wrong desk.
  • Defects on roads under liability get fixed at the contractor's cost, not the city's.
  • It can sit in front of the existing complaint system as a routing layer. It does not replace anything.

docs.title: Success measures
docs.text:
• Routing accuracy on test points checked by someone who knows the ward.
  • Share of the ward's recently built roads with known liability dates.
  • Time from photo to a correct, sourced answer.

docs.title: Risks specific to this idea
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Wrong agency named Show confidence and the alternative; let users correct it; corrections go to review, then into the graph Liability dates wrong Show only when extracted from a contract document, with the clause quoted Officer names out of date Route to the post; show the holder only with a "last verified" date Harassment of individual officers Post-based addressing; no personal phone numbers; rate-limit complaints per asset and merge duplicates

docs.title: Idea 5: Ward Lens
docs.text:
Ward scorecards that set spending against outcomes, checked by citizens on the ground.

Read 00-shared-foundation.md first.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
Money spent is an input. What residents care about is whether the drain floods, whether the school has teachers, whether the dispensary is open. Spending and outcomes are reported by different bodies in different units for different geographies, so nobody can say whether a ward that received more got more.

There is also no ground truth. A work is "completed" when the paperwork says so.

docs.title: What the user gets
docs.text:
• Ward scorecard: per sector (roads, drains, water, health, education, solid waste), the allocation, the spend, the works completed, and two or three outcome indicators, with the trend over years.
  • Fair comparison: per resident, per kilometre of road, per slum household, so dense and poor wards are not compared unfairly with rich ones.
  • Citizen verification: residents confirm or dispute a work's status with a geotagged photo. "Official status: complete. 14 citizen reports: 11 say incomplete."
  • Ask: "Which wards have the highest drain spending per kilometre and the most waterlogging complaints?"

docs.title: The semantic model
docs.text:
The graph holds the facts. A thin metric layer on top defines each indicator once, so the scorecard, the chat agent and any export compute it identically.

metric: road_spend_per_km
label: Road spending per km of road
numerator:   sum(Contract.value) where Work.category = 'roads' and FiscalYear = $fy
denominator: sum(Road.length_km)
grain: [AdminWard, FiscalYear]
unit: INR lakh per km
sources: [official]
caveats: "Excludes citywide projects such as the Coastal Road."

In the ontology, indicators are first-class:

(Indicator {code, label, unit, direction})          // direction: higher_is_better | lower_is_better
(Observation {value, period})-[:OF]->(Indicator)
(Observation)-[:FOR]->(AdminWard)
(Observation)-[:FROM]->(SourceDocument)
(Indicator)-[:MEASURES]->(Sector)
(BudgetHead)-[:SERVES]->(Sector)
(Work)-[:IN_SECTOR]->(Sector)
(CitizenReport {status_claimed, photo, at})-[:ABOUT]->(Work)
(CitizenReport)-[:BY]->(Reporter {reputation})

Sector is the bridge: budget heads and works roll up to sectors on the money side; indicators roll up to sectors on the outcome side. This is modelled on the RDF Data Cube idea of observations with dimensions, kept simple.

docs.title: Indicators to start with
docs.text:
Choose only those with a public source at ward level. Candidates:

Sector Money Outcome Roads Spend per km Pothole complaints per km; share of works past deadline Storm water drains Spend per km of drain Waterlogging complaints; flooding spots reported Solid waste Spend per resident Garbage complaints per 1,000 residents Health Spend per resident Dispensaries per 100,000 residents; reported dengue and malaria cases Education Spend per enrolled pupil Enrolment trend; pupil to teacher ratio Water Spend per connection Contamination and shortage complaints

Praja Foundation's annual reports and BMC's own published statistics are the likely sources for complaints and service indicators. Confirm coverage before promising any row of this table.

docs.title: Example queries
docs.text:
Money and outcome side by side for one sector:

MATCH (w:AdminWard)
OPTIONAL MATCH (w)<-[:LOCATED_IN]-(:Asset)<-[:IMPROVES]-(wk:Work)-[:IN_SECTOR]->(:Sector {code: 'drains'})
OPTIONAL MATCH (c:Contract)-[:FOR_WORK]->(wk)
WITH w, sum(c.value) AS spend
OPTIONAL MATCH (o:Observation)-[:FOR]->(w)
OPTIONAL MATCH (o)-[:OF]->(i:Indicator {code: 'waterlogging_complaints'})
RETURN w.code, spend, sum(o.value) AS complaints
ORDER BY spend DESC

Works where official status and citizens disagree:

MATCH (wk:Work {status: 'complete'})<-[:ABOUT]-(r:CitizenReport {status_claimed: 'incomplete'})
WITH wk, count(r) AS disputes
WHERE disputes >= 3
RETURN wk.title, wk.completed_on, disputes
ORDER BY disputes DESC

docs.title: Citizen verification design
docs.text:
• A report needs a photo taken in-app, with GPS within 50 metres of the work and a timestamp. No gallery uploads.
  • Claude vision checks the photo plausibly shows the work type and blurs faces and number plates before storage.
  • Reports are citizen-tier evidence. They never change the official status; they sit beside it.
  • A reporter's reputation rises when their reports agree with later official or majority evidence. Weight reports by reputation to resist brigading.
  • Three or more independent disputes on a "complete" work generate an item in the ward officer's digest.

docs.title: Implementation plan
docs.text: Phase Work Done when 1. Ward base Wards with population, area, road length, slum population share (Census and OpenStreetMap) Denominators for every ward 2. Money rollup Ward-level allocation and contract value by sector, from the Paisa Trail graph or from OpenCity's budget data Totals reconcile with the source 3. Outcome ingest Extract indicator tables from reports into Observations with source and period 6+ indicators across all wards 4. Metric layer YAML definitions and a small engine that compiles each to a query Scorecard and agent return identical numbers 5. Scorecard UI Ward page, city map shaded by a chosen metric, scatter of spend against outcome Demo script runs 6. Verification Photo report flow, checks, dispute query A live report appears on a work during the demo 7. Agent Chat over metrics with the caveats attached to each answer Evaluation questions pass

docs.title: Interpreting the numbers honestly
docs.text:
Spending and outcomes move together for many reasons. A ward may get more drain money because it floods. The interface must:

  • Never label a ward "inefficient" from one ratio.
  • Show trends over at least three years next to any comparison.
  • Attach the metric's caveats to every chart and every agent answer.
  • Describe patterns as questions ("spending rose 40% while complaints did not fall; what was built?") and link to the works so the question can be answered.

docs.title: Demo script
docs.text:
1. City map shaded by road spend per km. Pick the demo ward.
  2. Scorecard: money on the left, outcomes on the right, three-year trend.
  3. Ask: "Which three wards spent the most on drains per km and what happened to waterlogging complaints?" The answer includes caveats and sources.
  4. Open a work marked complete with several citizen disputes; show the photos.
  5. Submit a live report from a phone in the room (mock location).

docs.title: Success measures
docs.text:
• Number of indicators with full ward coverage and a cited source.
  • Agreement between the scorecard and hand calculations for three wards.
  • Number of verified citizen reports per work in a pilot ward.

docs.title: Why this is roadmap, not day-one
docs.text: Outcome data at ward level is the scarcest input and takes weeks to assemble and reconcile. Citizen verification only becomes meaningful with real users over time. The piece worth building on the day, if there is capacity, is the citizen verification flow on top of Paisa Trail's works, since it needs no new data.

docs.title: Preparation and day plan
docs.text: For the recommended build: Paisa Trail as the spine, Jawabdar as the front door, one ward, roads only.

docs.title: Before the event (16 to 20 November)
docs.text:
The single biggest risk is arriving without data. Everything this week reduces that risk.

Day Task Output Mon 16 Data spike. Open every source in 00-shared-foundation.md section 4 and record what is actually downloadable and in what format. On Mahatenders, open five BMC road tenders and note exactly what the detail, status and AOC pages show (07-tender-portals.md lists what to confirm). Email the organisers to ask what data the problem briefing will provide. A one-page source log: works / broken / needs login Mon 16 Choose the ward. Pick one a team member lives in, with visible road works and at least one non-BMC road. Named ward Tue 17 Database spike. Run HydraDB locally and Neo4j Community in Docker. Load 100 dummy nodes over Bolt with the neo4j Python driver. Run the queries from the idea files on both. Read HydraDB's cypher-compat.md for MERGE, date arithmetic and variable-length paths. Decision: HydraDB or Neo4j, written down with the reason Tue 17 Ontology v0. Write mco.ttl and SHACL shapes for the roads slice only. Generate the extraction JSON schema from it. Schema that validates one hand-written example Wed 18 Corpus. Download the roads budget pages, 40 to 60 tenders for the ward from Mahatenders with their BMC notice PDFs, any committee resolutions, the concretisation dashboard entries, ward boundaries, OpenStreetMap roads. Archive with hashes. data/raw/ with a manifest Wed 18 Gold set. Hand-label 10 documents. Write 30 evaluation questions with correct answers. eval/ folder Thu 19 Extraction v0. Run Claude over the corpus with the schema. Measure against the gold set. Fix the prompt, not the output. Accuracy number; loaded graph Thu 19 Org graph. Hand-build agencies, departments, posts and the issue routing table for the ward. "Who is responsible" query works Fri 20 Walk the ward. Photograph five roads in the graph. Note which facts the graph got right. Take the demo photos. Reality check and demo assets Thu 19 Agents. Run ant apply in managed-agents/, then civic_client.py ingest on ten documents. Fix what the first real run shows; tune the rubric. See 08-multi-agent-system.md. Agents created; one clean intake batch Fri 20 Skeleton app. Map, one trail view, and a chat panel backed by the Citizen desk agent. Something that runs end to end, however rough Fri 20 Freeze. Snapshot the database. Write the demo script. Prepare a one-page brief for teammates who join on the day. A build that works with no network

Check the event rules on pre-built work. If only work done on the day counts, treat the above as data preparation and research (normally allowed) and rebuild the app on the day from the plan. The data, ontology and gold set are the parts that cannot be made in eight hours.

docs.title: Team
docs.text:
Aim for four or five people. The event invites non-coders; use them.

Role On the day Graph and back end Loader, queries, graph tools in civic_client.py AI Agent files and rubrics, intake runs, evaluation Front end Map, trail cards, chat, mobile view Domain (policy person, journalist or resident) Verifies facts, finds the story, writes the complaint templates Lawyer, if available Reviews wording of anything naming a contractor; checks RTI and complaint drafts

docs.title: Day plan (21 November)
docs.text:
Adjust to the published schedule. Assumes roughly eight build hours.

Time Activity Briefing Listen for two things: what data the authorities can share, and what they say hurts most. Change scope to match. If they hand over data, one person starts ingesting it immediately. Hour 0 to 1 Team formation. Share the one-page brief. Agree the demo script first, then work backwards from it. Assign owners. Hour 1 to 3 Vertical slice. One road, end to end: map tap → trail → source page. Photo → responsible post → draft complaint. Ugly is fine. Hour 3 to 5 Widen. Load the full ward. Run the evaluation set. Fix the worst extraction errors. Add the liability period and the second-agency case. Hour 5 to 6 Languages and polish. Marathi and Hindi answers. Source drawer with highlighted quotes. "Allocated but not tendered" list. Hour 6 to 7 Feature freeze. Rehearse the demo three times. Record a backup video. Domain lead checks every figure that will appear on screen. Hour 7 to 8 Pitch deck: five slides (below). Buffer.

docs.title: Rules for the day
docs.text:
• Demo from the frozen local snapshot, not from live sources or venue wifi.
  • Any figure shown on screen must open to its source in one click.
  • If a feature is not working by the freeze, cut it from the demo and put it on the roadmap slide.
  • Keep the Neo4j container ready even if HydraDB is primary.

docs.title: Pitch (five slides, three minutes plus demo)
docs.text:
1. The question. A photo of a broken road in the ward. "Who built this, what did it cost, and who has to fix it?" Today that takes an RTI and thirty days.
  2. Demo. Photo to answer to drafted complaint. Then the money trail.
  3. How. One ontology, one graph, built only from documents BMC already publishes. Every fact cites its page.
  4. What the city gains. Fewer misrouted complaints; defects repaired at contractor cost while roads are under liability; an early-warning list of allocations not yet tendered.
  5. The ask. One ward office for a 90-day pilot, and tender and work-order data as files instead of PDFs. Roadmap: promise tracking, contractor red flags, ward scorecards.

docs.title: After the event
docs.text: When Step Week 1 Publish the ontology and the cleaned one-ward dataset under an open licence. Write up what was easy and what was not. Weeks 2 to 4 Expand to three wards. Automate weekly refresh. Add Vachan Tracker on the same graph. Month 2 Pilot Jawabdar with one ward office and one residents' association. Measure routing accuracy and time to resolution. Month 3 Legal review, then a limited release of Thekedar Graph to journalists and auditors. Begin Ward Lens indicators.

docs.title: Checklist to bring
docs.text:
• Laptop with the database snapshot, both database containers and the corpus stored locally
  • Claude credits activated; API key tested; agents applied and claude-lock.json committed
  • Demo photos with location metadata
  • Backup demo video
  • Printed one-page brief and the source log
  • Phone hotspot

docs.title: Tender portals: BMC and Mahatenders
docs.text: What the two official tender sites publish, how their identifiers work, and how to turn them into graph data. Checked on 15 November 2026. Items marked confirm were not seen directly.

docs.title: 1. Where BMC tenders live
docs.text:
BMC procurement is spread over three channels. A tender notice's header says which one applies.

Channel Address Role BMC portal portal.mcgm.gov.in / www.mcgm.gov.in, under For Partners → Tenders Publishes tender notices and corrigenda as PDFs. Viewing only. Mahatenders mahatenders.gov.in Maharashtra's e-procurement system (NIC GePNIC). Bids are submitted and opened here; awards are recorded here. GeM gem.gov.in Used for some goods and equipment purchases. Bid numbers look like GEM/2026/B/7825407.

History that matters for older data: BMC ran its own SAP SRM bidding system until the end of December 2023. BMC notices state that tenders moved to Mahatenders from 21 December 2023 and that SRM was closed to users after 30 December 2023. Works tendered before that date will not be on Mahatenders; only the BMC PDFs exist for them.

docs.title: What is there
docs.text:
• Tender notices as PDFs, in a predictable location and naming pattern:
https://www.mcgm.gov.in/irj/go/km/docs/documents/Tenders-New/ETH/ETH_8000113000_110826.pdf
https://portal.mcgm.gov.in/irj/go/km/docs/documents/Tenders/ETH/ETH_7000023382_041022.pdf
                                                            └┬┘ └────┬────┘ └─┬──┘
                                                      folder   bid number   date ddmmyy
  • The same files are served from several hosts: www, portal, r3app and crmapp under mcgm.gov.in.
  • Folders seen: Tenders/ETH (older) and Tenders-New/ETH (2026). Some files are named ..._Tender Notice.pdf or ..._Draft Tender.pdf instead of carrying a date.
  • Bid numbers are ten digits starting 7000…, 7200… or 8000….
  • Vendor manuals and instructions under Tenders/Tender Manuals/.

docs.title: What a notice contains
docs.text:
One 2026 notice was opened (a Disaster Management Department equipment purchase routed through GeM). Its index lists: e-tender notice, header data, preamble, instructions, general conditions of contract, technical specifications, bill of quantity, and annexures including an integrity pact, litigation history and pending criminal cases.

For works tenders, expect the header data to give department, ward or zone, description, estimated cost, earnest money, contract period and key dates, and the general conditions to hold the defect liability clause. Confirm on a roads notice from the demo ward.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• The tender listing page (/irj/portal/anonymous/qlTenders) is a SAP portal view that returned "not compatible with your browser" to a plain HTTP fetch. Open it in a real browser, or drive one with Playwright, to read the listing.
  • The PDFs themselves download directly once the URL is known.
  • Documents are long (the sample was 1.7 MB) and some are scanned. Send only the notice, header data and relevant conditions pages to Claude, not the whole file.
  • No award or payment information is published here.

docs.title: Public pages
docs.text:
All under https://mahatenders.gov.in/nicgep/app?page=<name>&service=page.

Page name Shows Use FrontEndTendersByOrganisation Every organisation with its count of active tenders Entry point per agency FrontEndLatestActiveTenders Active tenders Current pipeline FrontEndAdvancedSearch Search by id, title, reference, organisation, dates Targeted lookup FrontEndTendersByLocation Tenders by place Ward-level filtering, if location is filled in FrontEndTendersByClassification By product or work category Roads, drains and so on FrontEndLatestActiveCorrigendums Corrigenda Deadline and scope changes WebTenderStatusLists Stage of each tender after closing Bid opening, evaluation, award ResultOfTenders Award of contract (AOC) records Award and contractor WebCancelledTenderLists Cancelled and retendered Stalled works FrontEndTendersInArchive Closed tenders History FrontEndDebarmentList Debarred bidders Blacklisting

There is also an MIS reports site at gepnicreports.gov.in/eprocreports/maha/. It returned a server error when checked; try again, as it may offer aggregate reports without page-by-page browsing.

docs.title: What was observed
docs.text:
• Organisation list: columns are S.No, Organisation Name, Tender Count. BMC appears as "Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai" with 158 active tenders.
  • Other Mumbai agencies on the same portal (active tender counts): BEST 59, Public Works Department Mantralaya 38, MSRDC 24, MMRDA 12, CIDCO 12, MHADA 9, Public Works Special Projects Mumbai 3. This matters for Jawabdar: the same pipeline covers roads that are not BMC's.
  • Tender listings: Tender Title, Reference No, Closing Date, Bid Opening Date.
  • Results of Tenders: search by Tender ID or keyword; result columns are S.No, AOC Date, e-Published Date, Title and Ref.No./Tender ID, Organisation Chain, AOC.
  • Debarment list: columns are S.No, Bidder Name, Login ID, Product Category, Start Date, End Date; searchable by login id or PAN. The default view showed no records.
  • Captcha: the organisation list and the results search both require a captcha before showing data.

docs.title: Tender ID
docs.text:
Mahatenders ids follow the pattern seen in public document links:

2026_MCGM_1303610_1
 │     │      │    └ version (increments on retender)
 │     │      └ running number
 │     └ organisation code
 └ year

This is the best primary key for a Tender node from 2024 onward.

docs.title: Tender detail and award pages
docs.text:
GePNIC portals normally show, on each tender's detail page: organisation chain, tender reference number, tender id, tender category (works, goods, services), form of contract, tender value, earnest money, location and pincode, period of work in days, publication and closing dates, the inviting authority, and downloadable notice and bill-of-quantity files. The status and AOC pages normally list the bidders, the evaluation stages, the selected bidder and the awarded value.

These were not opened in this session because they sit behind the captcha. Confirm on five BMC tenders in the data spike. If the status pages do list all bidders, the bid-level red flags in 03-thekedar-graph.md become feasible.

docs.title: 4. Mapping to the ontology
docs.text: Portal field Graph Tender ID (2026_MCGM_…) Tender.id Tender reference number / BMC bid number Tender.ref_no, Tender.bmc_bid_no Organisation chain (organisation → department → division) Agency, Department, and (Tender)-[:ISSUED_BY]->(Department) Title, work description Work.title; road and ward names extracted by Claude into (Work)-[:IMPROVES]->(Asset) Tender category, form of contract Tender.category, Tender.contract_form Tender value, EMD Tender.estimated_cost, Tender.emd Location, pincode Candidate AdminWard Period of work Contract.duration_days, used to compute due_on Published, closing, opening dates Tender.published_on, closes_on, opened_on Corrigendum (Corrigendum)-[:AMENDS]->(Tender) with the changed field and both values Tender status stage Tender.stage, dated AOC date, selected bidder, awarded value Award, (Award)-[:TO]->(Contractor), Contract.value Bidder list Bid, (Contractor)-[:SUBMITTED]->(Bid) Cancelled / retendered Tender.status; (Tender)-[:RETENDER_OF]->(Tender) using the version suffix Debarment entry Blacklisting {from, to} on Contractor Defect liability clause in BMC notice DefectLiabilityPeriod

docs.title: Joining the two portals
docs.text:
A work appears on both sites under different numbers. Link them in this order and record which rule matched:

  1. The BMC bid number printed as the reference number on Mahatenders, or the Mahatenders id printed in the BMC PDF.
  2. Same department, same closing date, and same estimated cost.
  3. Claude compares titles for the remaining candidates and gives a reason; stored as a probable match.

docs.title: 5. Collection plan
docs.text:
The captcha is the site's access control for listings. Do not try to defeat it. Work with it:

Method How When Ask for the data Request a bulk export of BMC tenders and awards from the organisers or BMC's IT department First; the event has civic authorities in the room Assisted browsing A person opens the site in a Playwright-driven browser, solves the captcha once, and the script saves the listing and detail pages for the chosen organisation during that session at a slow, polite rate Pre-event corpus for one ward MIS reports Check whether the GePNIC reports site gives organisation-level tables If it is back up BMC PDFs Direct download once bid numbers are known from the BMC listing Notice text, conditions, liability clause Third-party mirrors Sites such as Public Services Map and InfraLens republish Mahatenders notices Discovery only; always cite the official page

Store every saved page with its URL, time and hash. The demo runs from that archive.

docs.title: Scope for the hackathon
docs.text:
• BMC, Roads and Traffic department, one ward, tenders from January 2024 onward.
  • Target: 40 to 60 tenders with detail pages, their AOC records where they exist, and the matching BMC notice PDFs.
  • Add 5 to 10 tenders from MMRDA, MSRDC or PWD touching the same ward, for the multi-agency case.

docs.title: 6. Effect on the five ideas
docs.text: Idea What the portals add Paisa Trail A stable tender id, estimated cost, award value and contractor from an official source. Budget code is still the missing hop. Vachan Tracker Tender stage and corrigenda give dated, official evidence of progress or slippage. Cancelled and retendered lists reveal stalled promises. Thekedar Graph AOC records for awards; debarment list for blacklisting; bidder lists if status pages show them. Jawabdar Period of work gives completion dates; BMC notice gives the liability clause; other agencies' tenders on the same portal settle whose road it is. Ward Lens Tender value by ward and category, where location is filled in.

docs.title: 7. Still not available from either portal
docs.text:
• The budget head a tender is charged to.
  • Payments made and measurement records.
  • Completion certificates and inspection reports.
  • Penalties imposed.

These need committee resolutions, press notes, the concretisation dashboard or RTI. The trail should show them as named gaps.

docs.text:

  • Mahatenders: tenders by organisation
  • Mahatenders: results of tenders
